column119:
14/Apr/12 1:34 AM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;The link hover colors on the current footer are the only thing that's mine -- there's
a footer redesign that's mostly done, but I'm holding it back until I finish the header
-- but we actually have two interesting problems going on here.

Problem 1 is the footer has 1em of padding on the top and 1em of padding on the bottom,
so even though the footer height gets set to the banner height -- say 222px, which
is the size of the Yuletide banner -- the actual height of the footer becomes 222px
+ 2em, and the collection banner tiles to fill that. (There's also 2px for the border,
but that doesn't matter here.)

Problem 2 is the footer has a min-height of 150px to accommodate the beta banner. So,
when we have a 100px banner like with Die ultimative deutsche Challenge Sammlung, the
min-height overrides the height, so we get a 100px background tiling to fill a 150px
+ 2em space.

There are a couple of semi-solutions I can think of, but the reason I say "semi" is
because they just cause it to break differently. If I get rid of the beta banner and
the padding in the redesign, I'm pretty sure that will fix it.

22/Jan/14 12:37 PM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;Fixed by https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/1499

This was not specific to PDF files. The error message was not showing up because returning
in a sub-method will only take you back to the main controller action method (which
would then try to return a pdf etc file and bomb out). 

Since we no longer have sub-methods in the downloads controller show method, that lets
the check for file existence work. 

To make it possible to test this without relying on a transient failure, I've added
a flag you can pass to the show method to make it skip generating the download.

AO3 (an interim fix before the merge tool is developed).

FishieMishie
Open Doors Chair

column1: Tag sets: Canonical tags add themselves to all fandoms they are canonical in when approved
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3045
What archive revision are you testing on? (See the latest release notes in
http://archiveofourown.org/admin_posts, for example 0.8.4.4).
0.8.13 (+0.8.13 test)

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:
http://archiveofourown.org/tag_sets/102

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Nom various fandoms eg ST:TOS and ST(2009) with different characters
2. Approve fandoms and characters
3. Notice that some of the characters are in both fandoms when they were only nommed
in one

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?
Characters to associate with only the fandom they were nommed in

Please use labels and text to provide additional information.
column122:
06/Sep/13 7:07 AM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;This is more complicated than it might seem alas!

1) Once a tag is approved and in the set, the nominations become extraneous -- they're
ephemeral, and we want to be able to trash them once the set is finalized, so we can't
use information in those nominations. Basically, the nominations are purely a tool
to help the moderator populate a tag set. If the moderator puts a tag in the set, it's
in the set. Tag set code doesn't "know" about nominations, in other words -- the tag
set code stands alone. I don't think it's a good idea to change this. 

2) Once tags are added to a set, we rely on the canonical information from the AO3
tag universe in order to establish the relationships between those tags -- this is
how characters get slotted into fandoms in the list by and large. We only use manual
tag associations for characters and fandoms that aren't already hooked up. 

As a result, the only way to NOT have a character tag appear in every fandom tag where
that character "lives" in the tag universe is if we allowed tagset moderators to turn
off using the canonical relationships entirely. But if they did that, they would have
to manually associate EVERY character they approved in EVERY fandom they wanted the
character to appear in. 

3) I am pretty sure (haven't actually tried this) that there is a workaround for particular
tags which would be to nominate and approve a new, non-canonical version of a tag that
specified the tag -- eg, "Captain Jack Harkness (Dr. Who Only)" -- and then set up
a tag set association for that non-canonical tag. 

Anyway, offering option #2 would be a substantial amount of work on our end, and it
would entail tons of work on the tagset moderator's end that I'm skeptical any actual
tagset moderator would really want to choose to do, given the existence of the workaround
in #3. 

I would lean towards just adding an explanation to the FAQ to clear up confusion, and
marking this WontFix.

- **Status changed**: `Design`
- **Labels added**: ADTAttentionRequired

16/Dec/12 11:54 PM;557058:a04c228c-7d70-4967-8583-25de929b4720;https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/1038

What was going on:
1) Select elements without any blank options (like the date selects inside the backdating
options section) will be set to their first option when jQuery "blanks" their values.
2) The JS which handles collapsible form sections (like the backdating section) tries
to blank the values of a section's inputs when that section is collapsed.
3) When the work form is rendered, a method decides whether or not the "Set a different
publication date" option should be checked. The method returns true if the work's created_at
date differs by at least a day from its published_at date.
4) A record's created_at date is set by the db's clock, which is in UTC time. A work's
published_at date is defaulted to Date.today as reported by ______ (Rails? The server?
I don't know), whose clock is in US EST time. So between midnight UTC and midnight
EST, a work's created_at and published_at date's can differ by a day.

So, during the times described in 4), 3) causes the backdate option to be autochecked.
The user then un-checks this option which they never wanted, collapsing the form section.
This triggers 2) which attempts to reset the date selectors, and the "selected" date
becomes 01/01/12 due to 1).

Changes:
- Added a condition to the JS "blanking" logic so that the date selectors are left
as-is when the backdate options section is collapsed.
- Removed the option "Set this publication date for the entire work", since a first
chapter's publication date cannot be set independently from its work's pub date anyway,
and that option was never rendered on the edit forms for any chapters whose pub dates
COULD be set independently from their work's pub date. i.e. "Set this publication date
for the entire work" was actually always true if its "parent" checkbox was checked,
and so had no real purpose as an option for the user.
- The checkbox labeled "Set a different publication date" now directly toggles the
work's .backdate field, and is no longer auto-checked.
- Added some logic to reset a work's pub date (which is really just its first chapter's
pub date) when a backdated work is un-backdated, or in case a user checks the backdating
option, changes the date, then unchecks the option.- **Status changed**: `SubmittedPullRequest`

column1: Add chapter number to comment notifications for multi-chaptered works
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3076*

*Site revision:*
Originally created for version 0.8.13.8, updated for version 0.9.252

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*

1. Receive a comment notification for a multi-chaptered work
2. Want to know what chapter it was on

*What is the expected output?*

The subject line should say, “[AO3] Comment on [Chapter #] of [Work Title]”.

The first line of the comment should say, “[Commenter] left the following comment on [Chapter #: Chapter Title] of [Work Title]:” and the chapter info should link to the relevant chapter.

The link to all comments should say, “Read all comments on [Chapter #] of [Work Title]”.

*What do you see instead?*

Instead, there is no chapter information mentioned.

*Notes*

Similar changes will be needed in the edited comment notification, sent comment notification, and comment reply notifications.

h2. Testing instructions

You need two users whose emails you can access.

# Log in as a user whose email you can access
# Set your preferences to receive copies of your own comments
## Hi, username! > My Preferences
## Uncheck “Turn off copies of your own comments”
## Press “Update”
# Post a work with a single chapter. Note its URL
# Post a work with multiple chapters. Do not give the first chapter a custom title. Give the second chapter a custom title. Note the work URL
# Log in as a different user whose email you can access
# Set your preferences to receive copies of your own comments
## Hi, username! > My Preferences
## Uncheck “Turn off copies of your own comments”
## Press “Update”
# Go to the work from step 3 and leave a comment on it
# Edit the comment
# Go to the work from step 4 and leave a comment on each chapter
# Edit the two comments
# Log in as the user from step 1
# Reply to the comments you left in step 7 and 9
# Edit the three comment replies

h3. Expected behaviour

* At step 7
** work creator receives comment_notification for a comment on work title. It should not mention a chapter
** commenter receives comment_notification for a comment on work title. It should not mention a chapter
* At step 8
** work creator receives edited_comment_notification for a comment on work title. It should not mention a chapter
* At step 9
** work creator and commenter each receive two comment_notifications, one per comment on the specific chapter. The comment on the untitled chapter should only mention the chapter number, the comment on the titled chapter should include the chapter title in the mailer body (but not the subject) 
* At step 10
** work creator receives two edited_comment_notifications, one per comment on the specific chapter. The edited comment on the untitled chapter should only mention the chapter number, the edited comment on the titled chapter should include the chapter title in the mailer body (but not the subject)
* At step 12
** work creator and original  commenter each receive a total of 3 reply notifications. As above, the notification for the single chapter work should not mention a chapter and the other two notifications should mention the chapter number in both subject and email body, while only the comment notification for the titled chapter should include the chapter title in the mailer body
* At step 13
** original commenter receive a total of 3 reply edited notifications. As above, the notification for the single chapter work should not mention a chapter and the other two notifications should mention the chapter number in both subject and email body, while only the comment notification for the titled chapter should include the chapter title in the mailer body

h1. Deploy notes

Mailer workers need to be restarted.

column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3130
Because pages served from the squid cache do not hit the Rails app, the hit counts for
those pages don't get added to the database. 

A rake task will run one time per day on otw3/4 to collect the squid cache hits and
add them to redis (from whence they will be added to the database by the existing sweep).


This should occur once time per day around 4am eastern time (after the logfiles are
rolled over) and will include the hits from the previous day midnight-midnight eastern
time. 

NOTE: because squid hits are not labeled with visitor, there is no way to distinguish
the same person loading a single work multiple times or visiting multiple chapters
of a single work. Therefore we will count all the hits. This will result in hit counts
going up faster.

column1: squid caching: guests should correctly see the adult warning and be able to skip it in future
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3132
Squid caching problem: if one guest goes to an adult work with the view_adult preference
already set in their session, they will load the squid cache with the work WITHOUT
the adult page meaning that any subsequent guests will see the work with no warning
even if they do NOT have the preference set.

Solution: we are now setting a cookie the first time a guest chooses the preference;
if this cookie is set, then the webserver will rewrite the URL to include ?view_adult=true
at the end automatically. Otherwise, guests will always get the "adult" page, meaning
that for guests, the cached version at .../works/123 will be the adult warning, and
the cached version at .../works/123?view_adult=true will be the actual work, and they
will be redirected to the second if they have the cookie set. 

This should not change behavior for logged-in users/admins. 

To test: 

1) Visit an adult work as a guest (you should get the "adult" warning) and choose "proceed"
2) Visit a SECOND adult work as a guest (you should NOT get the "adult" warning but
be sent directly to the work)
3) Clear your cookies and go back to the SECOND adult work. You should once again see
the adult warning. 
4) Have another guest who has already chosen not to see adult warnings also go to the
SECOND adult work. They should NOT see the adult warning.

Looking at the schema we have:

CREATE TABLE `kudos` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `pseud_id` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `commentable_id` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `commentable_type` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `created_at` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `updated_at` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `ip_address` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `index_kudos_on_commentable_id_and_commentable_type` (`commentable_id`,`commentable_type`),
  KEY `index_kudos_on_ip_address` (`ip_address`),
  KEY `index_kudos_on_pseud_id` (`pseud_id`)

IP address should be a 32bit int :)

From the performance book.

Another example is an IPv4 address. People often use VARCHAR(15) columns to store IP
addresses. However, they are really unsigned 32-bit integers, not strings. The dotted-
quad notation is just a way of writing it out so that humans can read it more easily.
You should store IP addresses as unsigned integers. MySQL provides the INET_ATON()
and INET_NTOA() functions to convert between the two representations.

11/Jul/12 4:04 PM;557058:8eb04462-c6aa-4b1b-b7b4-259ed44d3c0b;Hmm, not so easy as it might appear at first sight.

Currently kudos belong to a pseud. The kudos' name is considered the pseud name, if
present (or "guest" if not).

The RedisMailQueue queue_kudo stores only the name of the kudo to redis, to be picked
up by the mailer and delivered.

When the array of kudos givers is parsed by the deliver_kudos method in RedisMailQueue,
only those names are available, so when the mailer assembles the batch notification,
the link to the user cannot be reconstructed with any certainty - because pseud names
aren't unique, unlike user names, and at that point the link to the user is not known.

One solution would be to make kudos belong_to a user, instead of a pseud. (Kudos are
always sent as given by the default pseud of the kudos giver.)

Another solution would be for the name method of kudo to return the username (the user
login), instead of the pseud name. Then the link to the user could be easily made.- **Labels added**: Difficulty-Hard

column1: Setting expires headers appropriately
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3160
Expiry headers are used by a web application to tell a client how long a page is valid
for so it doesn't need to be re-feteched. Both simple web clients and web caches can
use this information to speed up displaying pages.

Currently squid lives between nginx and the unicorns. Currently the application sets
a big do not cache set of headers on all requests.

This is an example of the headers my I get when I am logged in.

HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
Server: nginx/0.8.54
Date: Tue, 26 Jun 2012 21:54:11 GMT
Connection: keep-alive
Status: 304 Not Modified
Etag: "900ef6255cfb05774b55fae27f2f1b16"
Cache-Control: max-age=0, private, must-revalidate

There is a relatively simple document at http://www.howtoforge.com/how-to-set-up-a-caching-reverse-proxy-with-squid-2.6-on-debian-etch-p2

And the following page explains how we tell squid to ignore what the application is
saying.

http://www.squid-cache.org/Doc/config/refresh_pattern/

So these are the policies we currently have:
refresh_pattern http://archiveofourown.org/admin/.* 1 1% 2
refresh_pattern http://archiveofourown.org/users/.* 1 1% 2
refresh_pattern http://archiveofourown.org/user_sessions.* 1 1% 2
refresh_pattern http://archiveofourown.org/admin_posts/.* 1 1% 2
refresh_pattern http://archiveofourown.org/passwords.* 1 1% 2
refresh_pattern http://archiveofourown.org/abuse_reports/new.* 1 1% 2
refresh_pattern http://archiveofourown.org/support.* 1 1% 2
refresh_pattern http://archiveofourown.org/downloads/.* 1 1% 2
refresh_pattern http://archiveofourown.org/signup/.* 1 1% 2
refresh_pattern http://archiveofourown.org/works/.* 1 1% 2
refresh_pattern http:// 25 90% 30 ignore-no-cache override-expire ignore-private	ignore-reload
override-lastmod ignore-no-store ignore-must-revalidate 

So we don't currently cache a large number of urls, and anything for a user we believe
is logged in.

I think to test this it will need to be on test ( where we would set up another nginx
instance so we could test the new features ) or we will need to work together to get
squid working for a webdev.

Looking at setting the expiry header in ruby the following pages look reasonable.

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/3117361/how-do-i-set-expires-header-when-using-send-data

If we are generating expires headers I would hope that it would be possible to change
the amount of time we set the expiry for without a redeploy. ( if you did use mysql
please make the query identical so it get answered by the query cahce but I would expect
one of the redis to be a better place to store the config. Unless we can have it in
a file and a restart of the unicorns to reload it ?

I was reviewing Ariana's pull request and noticed a few problems, but we'd like Open Doors' approval before we make any changes. :) 1. "alice ttlg, 852 Prospect’s archivist" uses a smart/curly apostrophe, which might cause display issues for some users. Is it okay if we change it to a regular apostrophe? 2. "As a result, alice ttlg, 852 Prospect’s archivist, has been looking for a more sustainable home for the archive, finding one in AO3." Using text like "here" for a link presents accessibility problems, since people who use screen readers often navigate from link to link, skipping the text in between. column27:

(See the version label in the footer, for example v0.8.13.8.) 0.8.21.3 If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen: For example, help boxes on http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/search What steps will reproduce the problem? 1. View a help box that instructs users to input text in hopes of achieving a specified result (eg help boxes on search page) What is the expected output? What do you see instead? The help boxes currently use em tags, which are used to place emphasis on text, to set off text that the user should input and text that should be returned. HTML has better tags for this: kbd should be used anywhere we're showing text a user should/has/can/etc input and samp should be used where we're showing likely/desired/example/etc output. Please use labels and text to provide additional information. For instance, we currently have:
Harry Potter will find Harry Potter and Harry James Potter but not Harry.
We would instead want:
Harry Potter will find Harry Potter and Harry James Potter but not Harry.
(You might also need to add samp to the CSS for styling -- I don't see it on a quick glance. I'd expect it to be in with kbd, tt, code, var, pre.)

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1.  User A posts multi-chapter story with User B added as a coauthor on some chapters
2.  User B chooses to edit one of the chapters they are not a co-author on, then clicks
either "Preview" or "Post without preview"
3.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

Expect edited chapter to post.  Instead get Error 500 and edits lost.

Please use labels and text to provide additional information.

I assume co-authors should be able to edit any chapter given that they can delete any
chapter or the whole work, and can edit the work's metadata.  If being able to edit
other chapters is not desired, a more informative error message should appear.
column124:
21/Aug/16 12:42 AM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;This errors because params[:chapter][:author_attributes][:ids] is nil here (line 268 of the chapters controller):

{code:none}
    # stuff co-authors into author attributes too so we won't lose them
    if params[:chapter] && params[:chapter][:author_attributes] && params[:chapter][:author_attributes][:coauthors]
      params[:chapter][:author_attributes][:ids].concat(params[:chapter][:author_attributes][:coauthors]).uniq!
    end
{code}

It'll work if you make it blank instead, like so, but surely there is a prettier solution:

{code:none}
    # stuff co-authors into author attributes too so we won't lose them
    if params[:chapter] && params[:chapter][:author_attributes] && params[:chapter][:author_attributes][:coauthors]
      # [:author_attributes][:ids] is nil when the person isn't a co-author on the chapter
      if params[:chapter][:author_attributes][:ids].nil?
        params[:chapter][:author_attributes][:ids] = []
        params[:chapter][:author_attributes][:ids].concat(params[:chapter][:author_attributes][:coauthors]).uniq!
      else
        params[:chapter][:author_attributes][:ids].concat(params[:chapter][:author_attributes][:coauthors]).uniq!
      end
    end
{code}

10/Apr/13 10:19 AM;557058:8eb04462-c6aa-4b1b-b7b4-259ed44d3c0b;We can't really fix this in a watertight way right now, because of the way the whole
is written from the ground up. The only proper solution would be posting direct-to-anon,
or true anonymous posting, both complex pieces of development.

What we could do reasonably quickly is to reduce the number of cases this happens for.

At the time the batch subscription notification is built, we could check if the current
creation being batched is a work belonging to the orphan_account, and if the subscription
being batched isn't *to* the orphan_account, skip that creation from the notification.

If the subscription is being built just as the work was posted, and before the creator
had the time to orphan it, this breaks down, but hopefully a partial solution soon
is better than a total fix way later?

Open Doors would like to update the notification e-mail that is sent when an archive is mass-imported into AO3; this one to non-AO3 users whose e-mail addresses are registered to the imported-archive but not to an AO3 account, to notify them that their stories have been imported and can be claimed. What is the expected output? New text for the email: You're receiving this e-mail because 852 Prospect, the Sentinel Adult Fiction Archive, has recently been imported by Open Doors into the Archive of Our Own, and we believe that the following fanworks belong to you. We'd like to give you a chance to claim (or delete) these stories if you want to. And if you don't already have an account under a different e-mail, we'd like to invite you aboard! 852 Prospect's software has become somewhat creaky over the years, to the point where all updates are now required by hand. As a result, alice ttlg, 852 Prospect’s archivist, has been looking for a more sustainable home for the archive, finding one in AO3. (You can read the rest of the announcement here, and find additional information on Open Doors' FAQ page. For any questions not answered in the FAQ or this e-mail, please contact Support.) All of these imported stories are locked to registered users only (to keep them out of Google searches), so your works will only be readable by logged-in users unless you choose to make them fully visible. By the current archivist's request, all unclaimed imported works will be unlocked and open to all visitors 3 months after the import, just like the original archive site. For help unlocking, orphaning, or deleting your works, please contact Support. <%= link_to("Claim or remove your works: ", claim_url(:invitation_token => @token)) %> <%= link_to(claim_url(:invitation_token => @token), claim_url(:invitation_token => @token)) %> The works uploaded include: <% @external_author.works.each do |work| %> <%= link_to(work.title.html_safe, work_url(work)) %><%= (work.fandom_string.blank? ? "" : " (#{work.fandom_string})") %> If these works don't belong to you, please don't delete them! Copy the above links and contact Open Doors so that we can move them for safekeeping. If these works do belong to you, but you don’t want them, you can claim them and then orphan or delete them. (For assistance, please contact Support.) To preserve rec lists and bookmarks, the imported archive's web addresses will redirect to the imported copy of these works. If you've already uploaded a copy of these stories, a merge tool is currently in development to combine the hit counts and reviews of both copies, while keeping only one story body (and preserving the redirect link). You may also request that Open Doors reset the redirect to point toward the pre-existing copy on AO3. To do so, please contact Open Doors with your AO3 account name, imported archive's account name, and links to both the original archive URL, and the URL of the fanwork designated as the redirect. If you have other stories on the imported archive under an e-mail address you can no longer access, please contact Open Doors with any information that can help verify your identity. 06/Sep/12 7:05 PM;557058:0670e11e-5036-4aae-af3f-d6ae02967b60;What's actually happening with this issue:

--Chapter updates won’t _ever_ cause the work blurbs in a tag listing to update.
--Posting a new work will make all blurbs in that tag listing update.
--The issue affects _all_ tag pages, including fandom, pairing, character, and additional
tags.

This can be replicated at will on Test and on Beta.  On Beta, the issue has been hidden
for more popular tags by the fact that new works are posted often.  However, it still
means that no chapter update will ever cause a work to appear at the top of its tag
lists.  Thus, the issue affects all authors and readers of multi-chapter works.

Steps to replicate:

1)	Post a new work.  Note that it’s at the top of the tag listing for anything it’s
tagged with (fandom, pairings, characters, and additional tags).
2)	Add a chapter to that work.  Note that the added chapter doesn’t show up in the
work blurb on any of the tag pages.
3)	Wait any length of time you like.
4)	Note that the fandom tag pages still don’t show the updated work blurb.  (The longest
I’ve seen so far personally is 8 days on Beta.)
5)	Post a new work tagged with the tag(s) in question.
6)	Note that immediately the tag listing pages for these tag(s) have updated work blurbs.
 The second chapter of the earlier work shows, along with the proper updated date.

For a detailed description of testing this on Beta, with screencaps, see https://otw.16bugs.com/projects/4911/bugs/238715

column137:
12/Sep/12 3:51 AM;557058:8eb04462-c6aa-4b1b-b7b4-259ed44d3c0b;feed_sweeper.rb:

  def after_update(work)
    if work.posted? && (work.posted_changed? || work.revised_at_changed?)
      expire_tag_feeds(work)
    end
  end

The feed_sweeper is only invoked from works_controller:
  cache_sweeper :feed_sweeper

The feed sweeper only observes works (observe Work) and only does expire_tag_feeds
when the update action of the works controller is invoked. Not when the work *object*
has been updated. It is not like a model observer.

Chapter updates do not touch the works controller, so they do not trigger expire_tag_feeds
at all.

The only things that trigger it are posting a new work, or changing the global revised_at
date on an already posted work.

does, no idea about spam bots...

column1: Clicking “edit tags” from a work saved as a draft takes you to a form where your only save option posts the draft
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3210
What archive revision are you testing on? (See the version label in
the footer, for example v0.8.13.8.)

v0.8.21.3

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1.  Create a work, Preview, then choose "Save Without Posting" to send that work to
your "Drafts" page.
2.  Go to the "Drafts" page and click the "Edit Tags" button on the work.
3.  Edit your tags, then look around for an option that will let you save these edits
without posting the draft.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

Expect to find a way to save your tag edits to the draft.  Instead find only choices
to cancel or to save the tag edits to the draft _while also posting it_.

Please use labels and text to provide additional information.

The Edit Work Tags form that comes up when clicking "Edit Tags" on a draft has three
buttons--Preview, Update, and Cancel.  Cancel cancels your changes.  Update keeps the
changes but causes the work to be posted.

Clicking Preview takes one to a preview of the work blurb with the choices Post, Edit,
and Cancel.  Cancel cancels your changes.  Edit takes you back to the editing form,
with the three buttons described above.  Post keeps the changes but causes the work
to be posted.

Thus, there is no way to edit the tags from the "Edit Tags" button without posting
the work.

Tags _can_ be edited without posting the draft by using the "Edit" button, previewing,
and then choosing "Save Without Posting".

column1: Adding works to a series or reordering its works does not update the series information in blurbs or meta
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3212*

*What archive revision are you testing on?*  otwarchive v0.8.21.3

h1. Scenario 1: Adding a work to a series does not update series navigation in other works' meta

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*

# Log in
# Create a new work in a new series
## Post > New Work
## Fill in required fields
## Check “This work is part of a series”
## Fill in “Or create and use a new one:” with the title of your series
## Press Post to post the work
# Add a second work to your series
## Post > New Work
## Fill in required fields
## Check “This work is part of a series”
## Choose the name of the series you just created from “Choose one of your existing series”
## Press Post to post the work
# Follow the “Previous Work” link on your newly-created work to return to the work from Step 2

*What is the expected output? What happens instead?*

The Series information in the meta at the top of the work from Step 2 consistently fails to acquire a “Next Work” link. It should get such a link.

Note that the “Series this work belongs to” section at the bottom of the work _does_ appear to get the “Next Work” link.

h1. Scenario 2: Reordering works in series does not update work blurbs or meta

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*

# Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Series
# Edit the series you want to edit (this issue is generally easier to observe if the series has at least 3 or 4 works)
# Reorder Series
# Use drag and drop to change the order of the works (entering numbers in the text fields will not reproduce the bug)
# Press Update Positions to save
# You’ll be taken back to the series' show page (e.g., {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/series/###}}), where you can see the blurbs for the works in the series

*What is the expected output? What do you see instead?*

I would expect the order of the works on the list to be as I made them, and the information of the blurb to reflect that reordering.

Instead, the blurbs contain incorrect information about their position. For example, there may be multiple blurbs that say “Part *1* of Series Title.” 

If you access the works themselves, the series information in the meta at the top of the work may or may not be correct. (It’s also worth noting that the meta at the top of the work might not match the “Series this work belongs to” section at the end of the work, e.g., the meta may say Part 3 while the end of the work may say Part 4.)

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3220
What archive revision are you testing on? 0.8.21.3

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?
User reports that the "remove tag" button is not findable using their screenreading
program. 

Issue:
The x for deleting isn’t a link, so you can’t tab to it, ergo it doesn’t work with
screen readers. The easiest thing to do would be to just add an a href=“#” around the
x, but that would just be a stopgap and not totally accessible (because you could delete
a tag, sure, but which tag are you deleting? and you’d have to know “x” meant “delete”).

Solutions:
I’d like to see it set up more like the warnings and categories tags. Keep the text
field for typing your tags on of course, but instead of just tossing the tags up above
the text field, display them in a field set below the text field, and with checkboxes
instead of an x. The checkboxes could be pre-checked, and unchecking the boxes would
remove the tags on save (rather than making them vanish as soon as you unchecked the
box).

Another suggestion:
Titled Checkboxes similar to the "Check to Remove" buttons on the Tag Wrangling pages
http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/tags/Testing/edit (also improves touch targeting)



Please provide any additional information below.
https://otw.16bugs.com/projects/4911/bugs/236265 (original report and initial discussion)

04/Aug/12 9:50 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;The best way to do it is pretty convoluted, unfortunately, but here's how I make skin
changes:

1. Log in to test archive.

2. Go to the public skins page: http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/skins

3. Find the skin you want to work with. In this example, I'll use Panda Madness.

4. Right click the skin name and open the link in a new tab or window. This is the
page that will show you the CSS for the skin. For Panda Madness, it's http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/skins/890

5. In another tab or window, open the Preview of the skin and scroll down to the footer
so you can see what it looks like. For me, it's http://archiveofourown.org/skins/890/preview
I see two problems. First, the text is white, which means it's pretty much unreadable
on the light greyish background. Second, when I hover over the links, they get a red
background, which makes the red link text hard to read.

6. Now look back at the page with the CSS and see if it provides any clues as to what
the footer should look like. For Panda Madness, I see that #900 is the desired color
for the links, so that means I want to remove the background color for the links' hover
state. From the CSS, I can't tell what color the footer text was supposed to be, so
I'm going to make it the same color as the rest of the page text.

7. In an entirely different browser log in with the test admin account (you can ask
for the log-in information in the coders chatroom). I like to do this in a separate
browser so I don't have to log in and out each time I want to check the changes I make
to the skin (there are admin-only styles that can screw up the skin if you preview
it while logged in as an admin).

8. While logged in as an admin, go to the edit page for the skin you want to change.
For Panda Madness, that's http://archiveofourown.org/skins/890/edit

9. Make whatever changes to the CSS that will correct the problems you noticed in steps
5 and 6. For Panda Madness, I'm adding #outer #footer ul {color: #2a2a2a;} and #outer
#footer .actions a:hover {background: transparent;} directly underneath #outer #footer
.actions a {color: #900;}

10. Click Update.

11. Back in the first browser, refresh the page on which you are previewing the skin
and make sure the changes solved the problem. If they didn't, go back to the browser
where you are logged in as an admin, make more changes, update, and refresh as needed.

12. Once you've resolved the issue, you'll need to comment on the Google Code issue
with the solution and set the issue status to DeployedToTest. It should include the
name and URL of the skin you edited, which lines you removed or changed, and which
lines you added and where. This is for two reasons. One, the admin who updates the
skin on beta will need instructions. Two, the skins on test archive get reset frequently,
so you may have to go back and make the changes a second time if the skins get reset
before the testers can check the issue.

When the testers have ensured that your changes look good, they can set the issue status
to PendingAttentionOnBeta so someone with admin access can update the skin on beta.
When the admin updates the skin, they can set the issue to NeedsAttentionOnBeta so
the testers and/or you can double-check that the changes were copied over correctly.

column119:
12/Aug/12 7:18 AM;557058:8eb04462-c6aa-4b1b-b7b4-259ed44d3c0b;Aha! This really is lupus-er, caching. Memcaching, to be precise.

In the _commentable partial, commentable can be a work or a chapter.

If looking at a chapter, this will load the kudos partial with the chapter as the commentable:

<%= render "kudos/kudos", :kudos => @kudos, :guest_kudos_count => @work.guest_kudos_count,
:commentable => commentable %>

The kudos partial uses the commentable's cache key:

  <% cache "#{commentable.cache_key}/kudos" do %>

which will be a chapter, in this case.

But the kudos sweeper only expires the fragment corresponding to the newly created
kudos' own commentable - which will always be a work, not a chapter.

expire_fragment "#{kudo.commentable.cache_key}/kudos"

The result is that fragments corresponding to chapters live forever - or for however
long unexpired memcache fragments live, anyway.

20/Nov/12 4:00 AM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;This issue occurs on any/all fields  that we do automatic HTML parsing on. 

eg: http://code.google.com/p/otwarchive/issues/detail?id=2544

I suggest as a solution that we instead create an "PARSER_PADDING" config setting (maybe
two? PARSER_PADDING_SHORT: 10, PARSER_PADDING_LONG: 100), set it to something generous
like 100, and wherever there is a length check, use "..._MAX + ArchiveConfig.PARSER_PADDING"
instead of just the _MAX field, but only use the _MAX field in the error message. 

That way the error will report the same length as the counter, and the extra allotment
will remain concealed from the user, which is the only way to avoid more confusion.
(ie, if you show "107 left" the user will still be just as confused when their 107-char
long line bombs because of added parsing.

column1: Series: Warn when adding anonymous work to series
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3232*
*What archive revision are you testing on? (See the version label in the footer, for example v0.8.13.8.)*
0.8.21.3

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*

# Create a new work that you make a new series for. This work is not anonymous.
# Create a second work: add it to the same series, and to an anonymous collection.
# Log out.
# View the series.

*What is the expected output? What do you see instead?*
It should be difficult for others to determine who has written an anon work. 

Instead: the bylines of the series and the anonymous work will show "Anonymous", but the byline of the non-anonymous work will show the actual creator, hinting at who "Anonymous" might be.

We want to add a flash message to warn users, when after the edit, the work (doesn't matter if it's anon or not) is in a series containing both anon and non-anon works:
{quote}
This work is in a series that contains anonymous works. Note that others may be able to guess who created the anonymous works in the series.
{quote}

[https://otw.16bugs.com/projects/4911/bugs/213920|https://otw.16bugs.com/projects/4911/bugs/213920]
[https://trello.com/c/4UhpokMa|https://trello.com/c/4UhpokMa]
column120:
24/Feb/20 8:13 PM;557058:f99670ac-6f0b-469b-bdfb-a9817a67932f;{quote}
Instead, when someone looks at your dashboard, they see your new anonymous series under Recent Series. Following the series link shows the title and link for your anon work, effectively destroying your anonymity.
{quote}
This will be fixed in AO3-5880.

However, user anonymity is still broken if we have a series with both anonymous and non-anonymous works. The bylines of the series and its anonymous works will show "Anonymous", but the byline of non-anonymous works will show the actual creators. To fix this, we have these options:

1. Add a warning after a work is edited to add a series: "Because this anonymous work is part of a series, others may be able to guess your identity." Allow the edit to succeed anyway.
2. Change the series byline to "anonymous, creator_name". We decided against this because (1) you still have a pretty good guess who "anonymous" can be and (2) this will contradict how bookmarked series search works (where a series is [indexed with creator "Anonymous"|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/e699d746172468ad819432753f72a41c6d99ff33/app/models/series.rb#L289-L291] if any work inside is anonymous).
3. Change all works in an anonymous series to be anonymous. This is unpredictable and we don't want to retroactively hide any works users never intend to hide.

We're going with option 1.

problem.

21/Jan/13 7:38 AM;557058:acee4fce-21cc-4291-8fa0-d813e774e099;Instructions for use:

Before you start, you will need:
- archivist's username (or new user, email and password)
- collection name and display title (or new ones)
- the name of the .pl database (probably ARCHIVE_DB.pl)
- the relative path to where the archive files are stored (relative to otwarchive/)

Run the rake task using "bundle exec rake massimport852:prospect[true]" (where true=send
email notifications and false=don't send email notifications)

*Notes:*
- Relatively few of the author email addresses are in the .pl file, so most are collected
from the HTML story files. Furthermore, the code only grabs the *very first* email
address in the story and assigns that as the author. (Some of the stories have dummy
emails embedded in the story, or list the email addresses of people who betaed etc,
so this was safer than harvesting all the email addresses and making them authors,
but may obviously lead to issues with stories that have multiple authors)

- If the harvested email address matches that of an AO3 user, the story is added automatically
to their works and a notification email is sent to say the story has been imported.

- If the harvested email address doesn't match that of an AO3 user, the story stays
assigned to the archivist (who is rather confusingly listed as the author in some views),
but the email address is used to create a new External Author. An invitation to claim
the stories associated with that email address is sent to the email address. 

If you want to play around or test before the live import, you can do the following:

- Amend the email addresses and logic in 852_replace_emails to mass replace emails
addresses in story files (or amend the "prospect" rake task to assign your email address
to all stories instead of parsing the files)

- Run the wipe_and_reload task to obliterate the collection, delete all the stories,
and then run the import process again. *Warning: this will send out deletion notifications
to all the email addresses associated with the stories in the collection, so make sure
you've substituted email addresses first!*

- Run the import with its send_invites parameter set to false; this will load the stories
without sending invites and notifications. (But deletion notifications will still be
sent out if you subsequently delete the collection!)

- 3781 Instructions don't toggle when switching between RTE and HTML editor
http://code.google.com/p/otwarchive/issues/detail?id=3781

- Browser spell check doesn't work in RTE (no issue, just something I noticed was broken)

It also sort of fixes:
- 3554 RTE Align Left button does not work, creating code that is stripped by the parser
http://code.google.com/p/otwarchive/issues/detail?id=3554

However, if you use the center tag in the HTML editor and switch to the RTE, you cannot
use the alignment buttons to remove it. This is because I told the RTE to use the align
attribute, which means it will not affect the center tag. So use align="center" instead
of the center tag if you plan on switching from the HTML editor to the RTE for the
purpose of using its alignment options. (It's probably not entirely unfixable, but
I haven't gotten quite that invested.)

It may fix but I cannot test:
- 3247 Centre button in RTE does nothing in Safari 5.0.4
http://code.google.com/p/otwarchive/issues/detail?id=3247

- 3253 Anomalies pasting some types of formatting from Word into the RTE 
http://code.google.com/p/otwarchive/issues/detail?id=3253

- 3257 Rich Text Editor not recognizing formatting on text from Windows RTF editors
http://code.google.com/p/otwarchive/issues/detail?id=3257

- 3267 Rich Text Editor (RTE) stripping formatting when pasting with certain combinations
of browser, operating system, and word processor
http://code.google.com/p/otwarchive/issues/detail?id=3267

This also adds a button for video embeds, as discussed in the AD&T e-mail thread "Update
RTE?" from 11 August 2013. If you look at the [example editor on the TinyMCE site](http://www.tinymce.com/tryit/full.php),
there are two tabs in the Insert/Edit Video popup. The General tab is geared toward
uploads, which isn't something we offer. The Embed tab is where you paste the embed
code just like you'd paste it into our HTML/plain text editor. Naturally, there's not
a way to configure TinyMCE to only use the Embed tab on the Media plugin.

One more thing: there is no longer a special Paste from Word button, since pasting
from Word is identical to pasting from everywhere else (this is true in our current
version as well, but the button is still there). If wanted, I can add a plain Paste
button (there are also Copy and Cut buttons) so we don't rely on users knowing the
keyboard shortcut for pasting.- **Status changed**: `SubmittedPullRequest`

- 3291 Rich Text Editor (RTE) creates broken links to works on the Archive http://code.google.com/p/otwarchive/issues/detail?id=3291

- 3781 Instructions don't toggle when switching between RTE and HTML editor
http://code.google.com/p/otwarchive/issues/detail?id=3781

It also sort of fixes:
- 3554 RTE Align Left button does not work, creating code that is stripped by the parser
http://code.google.com/p/otwarchive/issues/detail?id=3554

However, if you use the center tag in the HTML editor and switch to the RTE, you cannot
use the alignment buttons to remove it. This is because I told the RTE to use the align
attribute, which means it will not affect the center tag. So use align="center" instead
of the center tag if you plan on switching from the HTML editor to the RTE for the
purpose of using its alignment options. (It's probably not entirely unfixable, but
I haven't gotten quite that invested.)

It may fix but I cannot test:
- 3247 Centre button in RTE does nothing in Safari 5.0.4
http://code.google.com/p/otwarchive/issues/detail?id=3247

- 3253 Anomalies pasting some types of formatting from Word into the RTE 
http://code.google.com/p/otwarchive/issues/detail?id=3253

- 3257 Rich Text Editor not recognizing formatting on text from Windows RTF editors
http://code.google.com/p/otwarchive/issues/detail?id=3257

- 3267 Rich Text Editor (RTE) stripping formatting when pasting with certain combinations
of browser, operating system, and word processor
http://code.google.com/p/otwarchive/issues/detail?id=3267

This also adds a button for video embeds, as discussed in the AD&T e-mail thread "Update
RTE?" from 11 August 2013. If you look at the [example editor on the TinyMCE site](http://www.tinymce.com/tryit/full.php),
there are two tabs in the Insert/Edit Video popup. The General tab is geared toward
uploads, which isn't something we offer. The Embed tab is where you paste the embed
code just like you'd paste it into our HTML/plain text editor. Naturally, there's not
a way to configure TinyMCE to only use the Embed tab on the Media plugin.

One more thing: there is no longer a special Paste from Word button, since pasting
from Word is identical to pasting from everywhere else (this is true in our current
version as well, but the button is still there). If wanted, I can add a plain Paste
button (there are also Copy and Cut buttons) so we don't rely on users knowing the
keyboard shortcut for pasting.- **Status changed**: `SubmittedPullRequest`

column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3297
Add a database index for chapters on work_id and position. This is a very common query
that we use to get the first chapter of a work:

SELECT `chapters`.* FROM `chapters` WHERE (`chapters`.work_id = ?) ORDER BY position
ASC LIMIT ?

We also do similar queries to get the chapters in order elsewhere. It's not terribly
slow, but it could be faster, so there's no reason for it not to be.

While doing this, please get rid of one of these:

  add_index "chapters", ["work_id"], :name => "index_chapters_on_work_id"
  add_index "chapters", ["work_id"], :name => "works_chapter_index"

Dunno why we have a duplicate there, but we only need one.

The short of it is, mysql / mariadb doesn't need to look at all the items, just a subset
of the data. Like, if you had 100 students, 5 of them have blue hair, and you wanted
to find the ones with blue hair and green eyes.

column1: Make the callbacks asynchronous
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3307
Certain requests, such as trying to re-wrangle/change the canonicals of tags with lots
of subtags/associated works, time out with 502s and can only be done by a database
admin, not possible over the web.

We need to make the callbacks asynchronous, so it doesn't try to move all the tags
and fix all the works before the next page loads, but instead does the work in the
background. This is especially needed because we also need to reindex the search results

14/Nov/12 10:54 AM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;OK, update: this was not in fact related to the async code or to the number of works
on a tag, but to the search engine reindexing, which wasn't being fired off for subtagged
works. 

The search engine should now be told to reindex results for all works and bookmarks
tagged even in subtags and subtag synonyms. A bunch of the code in the tag model had
to be touched for this so sadly it needs a really good banging. :/ 

The reindexing of works and bookmarks will also now have a batched delay (firing off
every 7 minutes and every 13 minutes respectively) for performance. 

To test: 

- find some tags that have a bunch of subtags and synonyms, ideally where the subtags
themselves have subtags and synonyms
- with each of those tags, try one of the following: 
* give one a new synonym and make sure all the syns and subtags move over (on the edit
page) and all the works move over (on the works page)
* give one a new meta tag and make sure it and all its subtags and works move over
* remove the subtags and make sure all the subtagged works go away
* remove a synonym and make sure the synonym-tagged works go away

Remember that the works pages will NOT update right away -- it will only happen once
the reindexing completes. To be safe give it 10 minutes and if it hasn't happened,
it's not working. 

BACK END NOTES FOR DEBUGGING:

*** If the synonyms/subtags don't appear on the edit page, Resque may not be running.


*** If the syns/subtags appear on the edit page, but the works don't refresh, check
in console to see if the work ids have been put into redis: 

> $redis.smembers("search_index_work")

in which case the rake task rake search:reindex_works may not be getting run by cron,
try running it manually and see if it works.

h1. JAWS

*Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3312*

*What archive revision are you testing on?*

0.9.1.4

/works/new 

*What browser / OS has this been witnessed on?* 

Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; MSIE 9.0; Windows NT 6.1; Trident/5.0; MAAU; MAAU)
Firefox, Chrome, same platform

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*

1. enable JAWS
2. attempt to enter a tag

*What is the expected output? What do you see instead?*

"Using JAWS13, the specific problem I’m having is in the selection of fandom/characters/pairings etc., where you need to start typing in order to choose suggestions. These fields are entirely invisible in Firefox and Chrome, but in internet explorer I am able to start typing into the field (though it is read as a menue). I can not, however, choose a selection from the subsequent list, nor can I read the list of suggestions without exiting forms mode."

After testing the suggestion found by front-end lead ([https://groups.google.com/d/msg/jquery-a11y/tYyNUyn4wYI/97fqtbGZ2OoJ),|https://groups.google.com/d/msg/jquery-a11y/tYyNUyn4wYI/97fqtbGZ2OoJ),] user confirms that the new jQuery UI autocomplete ([http://view.jqueryui.com/master/demos/autocomplete/default.html|http://view.jqueryui.com/master/demos/autocomplete/default.html]) is compatible. This will require an update to the jQuery back-end as well.

*Please provide any additional information below.*

[https://otw.16bugs.com/projects/4911/bugs/242444|https://otw.16bugs.com/projects/4911/bugs/242444]

h1. VoiceOver (macOS Catalina)

*Steps to reproduce:*

# Search > Works
# [Enable VoiceOver|https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/use-accessibility-features-mh35884/mac]
# Tab until you land in an autocomplete field, e.g. “Fandoms”

*What should happen & what happens instead:*

When you enter the field, VoiceOver will give you a lot of information about the field, and the information will end with some instructions: “Type text, or to display a list of options, press Control - Option - Space.”

After you press Control - Option - Space and enter some text, you _should_ be able to press the down arrow on your keyboard to make VoiceOver read through the suggestions. This does not happen. In fact, nothing happens other than your text being entered.

*Notes:*

The default instructions are a bit confusing because they suggest you can get a list of options before you type, but it’s _probably_ familiar to people—the search box on the Google homepage behaves the same way. However, to be safe, I’m going to make it read the little, “Start typing for suggestions\!” prompt to give people a nudge in the right direction. If it ends up being annoying, we can take it out.

It reads the suggestions a bit awkwardly, too, pausing slightly around the parts of words that match the input, e.g. if you enter “Te,” it might read “Teen Wolf (TV)” as “Te en Wolf (TV).” I thought maybe I could stop that by removing the {{b}} tag on the highlighted part and instead just using a {{span}}, but no dice. I’m leaving it with the awkward reading for now since the alternative seems to be taking the highlighting out.

15/Nov/20 6:06 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;[https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/3922|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/3922|smart-link] 

I’ve made a pull request to revert part of the changes:

* Updates the JavaScript responsible for the autocomplete so screen readers can interact with the suggestions. I've based this on [the first example on the W3's combobox with listbox examples page|https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-practices/examples/combobox/aria1.1pattern/listbox-combo.html].
** I've moved {{role="combobox"}} and {{aria-expanded}} onto the parent of the {{<input>}}. Having them directly _on_ the {{<input>}} meant that iOS VoiceOver didn't recognize it as a box you can type in.
*** I've also made it so {{aria-expanded}} is set appropriately depending on whether or not the dropdown containing suggestions or tips is present.
** I've added the recommended {{aria-owns}} and {{aria-haspopup}} attributes and values to the combobox, the {{aria-controls}} attribute to the text field, and {{aria-labelledby}} to the listbox. tbh, I didn't see that they made any difference, but they're there now.
** When you use the arrow keys to navigate the options, an {{aria-activedescendant}} attribute referencing the selected option will be added to the {{<input>}}. The selected option will also get the attribute {{aria-selected="true"}}.
*** Note: if you're using a mouse and hover in certain places, it's possible for the {{<input>}} to acquire the {{aria-selected}} and everything else added by the {{select_dropdown_item}} function. I suspect this has to do with the somewhat peculiar HTML structure that sticks the text field in a {{<li>}}, but I'm not sure. You can see it on production, too -- a tiny bit of visible red to the left side of the field if you wave the mouse around just so. I'm just... not going to touch that right now.

However, it keeps these:

* Uses HTML5 {{data-*}} attributes for the autocomplete's custom attributes. This means we don't get as many validation errors on our HTML now. 🎉
* Removes the {{title}} attributes on the work form tag section's autocomplete fields. (AO3-5831)
* Makes sure that if the original {{<input>}} has an {{aria-describedby}} attribute, it is placed on the new {{<input>}} as well.
* Increases the timeout for searching when entering text. This makes autocomplete work better on iPhones, which also makes this easier to test on such devices. (AO3-5833)

column130:
01/Sep/13 6:40 PM;557058:8eb04462-c6aa-4b1b-b7b4-259ed44d3c0b;Current theory:

1. work.rb
   has_many :taggings, :as => :taggable, :dependent => :destroy

2. tagging.rb
  before_destroy :delete_unused_tags

  # Gets rid of unwrangled tags that aren't tagging anything else and which aren't
  # already deleted  
  def delete_unused_tags
    return if tagger.nil?
    tagger.destroy if (tagger.unwrangled? && tagger.taggings == [self])
  end

So the deletion of the work (or draft) that was the only thing keeping the tag on the
Archive (if no one had had time / the chance to wrangle it) triggers the destruction
of the tag itself.

Because, you see, posting a work using that tag turns it into a Real Tag (from a tag
nomination), so it gains the strengths and vulnerabilities of the flesh tag.

Why does it not stay a nomination? Exercise left to the reader. ;-) ('tis almost 3
am.)

column120:
09/Jan/13 5:15 PM;557058:56c6aaf0-abec-4140-88a3-59aa2f24c990;This is wider-spread than just on the public tag pages; it happens on the tags of works
themselves. It is consistently reproducible in certain cases:

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Go to a work in a collection from the collection page - make sure that the link
is to ao3.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME/works/####
2. See that the tag links in the header box link to the tags within the collection
(e.g. ao3.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME/tags/TAGNAME/works rather than just ao3.org/tags/TAGNAME/works)
3. Go to the main listing of the work http://archiveofourown.org/works/###
4. See that the tags still link to ao3.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME/tags/TAGNAME/works
rather than the expected ao3.org/tags/TAGNAME/works

(The reverse will happen on occasion, too, that the tag-links on works within the collection
will lead to the full works list rather than the collections-limited list.)

This problem is somewhat self-correcting - after waiting a time (~30 minutes) and reloading
the tags will 'reset' to what they should be (except that when they do it means the
tags on the other version of the work are wrong - e.g. the tags on the collection-version
of the work will link to the main tags.)

The same problem also occurs in the Works index listings (in both directions; regular
index listings will be linking to the collection-tags, or else the collection tags
will be linking to the full list) For instance, fandom tags on Sarken's work pages:
http://archiveofourown.org/users/sarken/works?page=3 often (erratically) link to the
collection-specific versions (on works that are in collections; works not in collections
do not appear to have altered tags?)

(also note that the works listing and tags listing on a work are unrelated - tags may
be linking correctly on the work itself but incorrectly on the works listing.)

column124:
15/Nov/13 3:16 AM;557058:8eb04462-c6aa-4b1b-b7b4-259ed44d3c0b;Hi creidieki, and thanks for taking a look at this!

@collection is an instance variable that, if not nil, refers to the collection in the
context of which the tag is being linked to. The tag doesn't "have" a collection or
more, and a collection doesn't "have" tags.

So, if a collection_id parameter is present, a before filter in various controllers,
load_collection, will create @collection for the collection with that id. And then
that variable @collection will be available for whatever action is being performed,
and any views invoked by the action.

Which means that any tag links generated when a tag (or work?) has been accessed through
a collection will contain that collection (will send that collection_id parameter forth).

This is needed when one wants to browse within the collection.

But those links are cached, and especially cached in bulk on a tag's show page: the
children are cached. The cache key is the same, however, so if a bunch of child tags
were cached in the collection context (the child tags are ALL the tag's children, whether
any works / bookmarks with the tag appear in the collection or not - this is not checked)...
the same cached chunk is being used in ANY context that tag is loaded.

/o\

So that's what happens. (It's always caching. >.<)

So thank you, thanks to your comment I finally understood how the bug happens. :)

column1: Add help pop up next to Top Ten and Other Tags titles in new filters

column27: Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3370 What archive revision are you testing on? otwarchive test-0.9.2.18 If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen: any page with filters There's no help pop up, and thus no easy way to learn how to use the filters. To fix this issue add help pop ups to both places, both leading to this text: The Top 10 drop down filter boxes will show the top ten most popular tags for each category. To filter by any other tags, you need to use the 'Other Tags' field below them. If the tag that interests you isn't in the Top 10, scroll down to the 'Other Tags' field, and start typing the tag you need -- all types of tags are valid here, and you can add as many tags as you want. The autocomplete will help you find the common (canonical) version of the tag. Use the forms that show up in the auto-complete (common or canonical forms) in order to take full advantage of the wrangled tagging structure, and find all works tagged with tags with synonymous meanings and subtags. You can enter tags that aren't in the auto-complete, but in that case the filters will do a simple text match and may bring up unexpected results. The "Search within results" field will text-match more accurately, especially in the case of relationship tags and other tags with '/' or other non-text characters. Choosing any tag in the Top 10 or writing in a tag in the 'Other Tags' field will do an 'AND' search with all the tags you select. This means that if you're filtering the works tagged with the F/F category, select the Teen and Up Audiences rating, the common (canonical) Romance tag in the Additional Tags dropdown, and type or select the common (canonical) tag Drama in the Other Tags field, only works tagged with all these tags will appear. To exclude things or get results with Tag A OR Tag B, use the 'Search withing results' field. To look up tags and see which ones are common (canonical) use the Tag Search. To read the guidelines the Tag Wranglers use to mark tags common (canonical), among other things, or to better understand the AO3-specific vocabulary for tags, read the Wrangling Guidelines.

work in some versions of IE so using both the white-space and word-wrap is the best

column136:
14/Dec/13 6:42 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;*nods*

In the majority of instances, word-wrap and word-break both work, just a little differently:
word-wrap lets the word get as long as it can be within the container, even if it means
pushing it onto another line, while word-break only lets the word get as long as it
can on the line, effectively letting us choose between adhering a bit closer to the
users' input or prettying up the input to preserve the layout a bit more. For example,
if the user puts in a 12-character word and line 1 can fit 10 characters, but line
2 can fit 20 characters, word-wrap will put that word on the second line, while word-break
will spilt it across two lines.

The problem in the inbox isn't with wrapping the text, but with the default display
of the fieldset element. While it's possible to make the text in the inbox wrap with
a combination of break-word, pre-wrap, and an explicit width on the container, the
fieldset element won't shrink accordingly, so you're still left with horizontal scrolling
for the entire window. There are a variety of workarounds, all of which have down sides.
I opted for horizontal scrolling for the inbox form's content because it'll do something
to improve the experience for Firefox users who are viewing an inbox page with an overly
long word (they'll be able to use the filters on that page), but it won't have a negative
affect on that page for anyone else (or, worse, a negative affect on all inbox pages).

column27:

Searching (in any field, Title, tag search, etc) does not properly match for "and"
"not" "or" "of" and a variety of other short words, even when these words are enclosed
by quotation marks and included with other words.  For example:

Searching for the phrase "secrets are told" in the Any Field box brings up works with
"no secrets and told each other" and "secrets get told".

Tag searching for "Not Porn" finds all tags using 'porn'.

column123:
15/Mar/19 5:58 PM;557058:f99670ac-6f0b-469b-bdfb-a9817a67932f;As of the ES6 upgrade, titles of works are indexed using the [simple analyzer|https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/6.6/analysis-simple-analyzer.html] which doesn't remove any stop words by default.

[Searching for "And Heaven Too"|https://archiveofourown.org/works/search?commit=Search&page=1&utf8=%E2%9C%93&work_search%5Bbookmarks_count%5D=&work_search%5Bcharacter_names%5D=&work_search%5Bcomments_count%5D=&work_search%5Bcomplete%5D=&work_search%5Bcreators%5D=&work_search%5Bcrossover%5D=&work_search%5Bfandom_names%5D=&work_search%5Bfreeform_names%5D=&work_search%5Bhits%5D=&work_search%5Bkudos_count%5D=&work_search%5Blanguage_id%5D=&work_search%5Bquery%5D=&work_search%5Brating_ids%5D=&work_search%5Brelationship_names%5D=&work_search%5Brevised_at%5D=&work_search%5Bsingle_chapter%5D=0&work_search%5Bsort_column%5D=_score&work_search%5Bsort_direction%5D=desc&work_search%5Btitle%5D=And+Heaven+Too&work_search%5Bword_count%5D=] correctly brings up titles such as "And Heaven Too", "all this and heaven too", and only variations in the word order on the 6th page (e.g. "Heaven and Hell Run on Paperwork Too").

Similarly, tag names are indexed with a customized [standard analyzer|https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/6.6/analysis-standard-analyzer.html] (which can have stop words, but has none by default). So [searching for "not porn"|https://archiveofourown.org/tags/search?utf8=%E2%9C%93&query%5Bname%5D=not+porn&query%5Btype%5D=] finds only tags with both terms. Results may be a bit against the spirit of the search (e.g. "again not explicitly porn but kink and literally no plot") but hey, we're not outright returning porn tags.

I think this is fixed.
column124:
15/Mar/19 7:29 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;[A search for the title and things that go bump in the night|https://archiveofourown.org/works/search?utf8=✓&commit=Search&work_search%5Bquery%5D=&work_search%5Btitle%5D=and+things+that+go+bump+in+the+night&work_search%5Bcreators%5D=&work_search%5Brevised_at%5D=&work_search%5Bcomplete%5D=&work_search%5Bcrossover%5D=&work_search%5Bsingle_chapter%5D=0&work_search%5Bword_count%5D=&work_search%5Blanguage_id%5D=&work_search%5Bfandom_names%5D=&work_search%5Brating_ids%5D=&work_search%5Bcharacter_names%5D=&work_search%5Brelationship_names%5D=&work_search%5Bfreeform_names%5D=&work_search%5Bhits%5D=&work_search%5Bkudos_count%5D=&work_search%5Bcomments_count%5D=&work_search%5Bbookmarks_count%5D=&work_search%5Bsort_column%5D=_score&work_search%5Bsort_direction%5D=desc] (no quotes) brings up 11 works that contain all of those words including “and”, contrasted to [searching for just things that go bump in the night|https://archiveofourown.org/works/search?utf8=✓&commit=Search&work_search%5Bquery%5D=&work_search%5Btitle%5D=things+that+go+bump+in+the+night&work_search%5Bcreators%5D=&work_search%5Brevised_at%5D=&work_search%5Bcomplete%5D=&work_search%5Bcrossover%5D=&work_search%5Bsingle_chapter%5D=0&work_search%5Bword_count%5D=&work_search%5Blanguage_id%5D=&work_search%5Bfandom_names%5D=&work_search%5Brating_ids%5D=&work_search%5Bcharacter_names%5D=&work_search%5Brelationship_names%5D=&work_search%5Bfreeform_names%5D=&work_search%5Bhits%5D=&work_search%5Bkudos_count%5D=&work_search%5Bcomments_count%5D=&work_search%5Bbookmarks_count%5D=&work_search%5Bsort_column%5D=_score&work_search%5Bsort_direction%5D=desc] (again, no quotes), which brings up 157 words. It’s definitely searching for “and” now.

Entering [and angst in the tags field of work search|https://archiveofourown.org/works/search?commit=Search&page=1&utf8=✓&work_search%5Bbookmarks_count%5D=&work_search%5Bcharacter_names%5D=&work_search%5Bcomments_count%5D=&work_search%5Bcomplete%5D=&work_search%5Bcreators%5D=&work_search%5Bcrossover%5D=&work_search%5Bfandom_names%5D=&work_search%5Bfreeform_names%5D=and+angst&work_search%5Bhits%5D=&work_search%5Bkudos_count%5D=&work_search%5Blanguage_id%5D=&work_search%5Bquery%5D=&work_search%5Brating_ids%5D=&work_search%5Brelationship_names%5D=&work_search%5Brevised_at%5D=&work_search%5Bsingle_chapter%5D=0&work_search%5Bsort_column%5D=_score&work_search%5Bsort_direction%5D=desc&work_search%5Btitle%5D=&work_search%5Bword_count%5D=] (still no quotes) appears to bring up only items that are tagged with a tag contain both “and” and “angst”. The tag probably shouldn’t be listed twice.

Likewise, [a tag search for not au|https://archiveofourown.org/tags/search?utf8=✓&query%5Bname%5D=not+au&query%5Btype%5D=] turns up only tags with both the words “not” and “au.”

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1.  When creating or editing the Challenge Settings for a prompt meme, set "Number
of prompts per signup" Required to a number greater than that for Allowed
2.  Hit "Update"
3.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

The blue-backgrounded message at the top of the form says:

If you set the "Required" value higher than the corresponding "Allowed" value, we will
automatically assume that you want the allowed value to be the same as the required
value. You only need to manually set the "Allowed" number if you want more allowed
than required.

So, I'd expect to get a prompt meme with Required and Allowed both set to the number
I entered for Required.  Instead I get a prompt meme with the settings as I entered
them.

Please use labels and text to provide additional information.

A prompt meme set up with Required > Allowed is impossible to sign up for.  The Signup
form has only the number of prompts allowed available, so filling it out completely
and then submitting it always gives the error:

Sorry! We couldn't save this ChallengeSignup because:

You must submit between <Required> and <Allowed> requests to sign up for this challenge.
You currently have <Allowed>.

If you set Allowed to zero (regardless of what you set for Required), this issue http://code.google.com/p/otwarchive/issues/detail?id=2476
makes it so you get an error message.  However, for any non-zero Required number, it
would make more sense to simply set Allowed=Required, as the form text implies will
happen.

Note that leaving Allowed blank causes it to be set to zero rather than to the value
of Required (on Beta).

Here are the search tips:

* I expect to get works tagged with arthur/merlin
* At first glance, it looks like I get just that! But that's just a trick -- it's actually
giving me results tagged with Arthur or Merlin, and it just happens that many of those

words: >1000 
* I expect to get works longer than 1,000 words.
* I get no results. (Note: This is a deeper problem and is getting its own issue.)

words: 100
* I expect to get works of exactly 100 words.
* I get no results. (Note: This is a deeper problem and is getting its own issue.)

tag: buffy gen teen "no archive warnings"
* I expect to get gen Buffy works with no warnings.
* I get mostly gen, teen-rated Buffy works with no warnings, but I also get the occasional
multi work and the occasional work tagged with only "Author Chose Not To Use Archive
Warnings." The multi thing is expected, since some works are tagged Gen and F/M (or
F/F or...). To stop the only "Author Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings" from turning
up, it should probably say "no archive warnings apply," since that's the full name
of the tag.
 
tag: lex slash (mature|explicit)
* I expect to get things tagged with lex and slash and rated only mature or explicit.
* I get no <del>satisfaction</del> results.

"cerulean orbs"
* I expect to get things with cerulean orbs somewhere in the blurb.
* I do get the two works tagged with "cerulean orbs," but I suspect this is leftover
from when we did full-text search, since it's not something particularly likely to
appear in the summary, tags, title, etc.

26/Nov/12 8:00 PM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;The problem here is that the work indexing doesn't get triggered to be refreshed based
on changes in hit counts, but only based on kudos, comments, or bookmarks. This makes
sense from a performance standpoint but is obviously producing confusing results. :/


Possible solutions: 

- reindex on hitcounts at staggered intervals, perhaps 1x/hour, so works don't constantly
get reindexed

- display the hitcount being sorted-on and not the actual hitcount (which would be
visible on the work itself

- both

column1: works index pages cache needs to be invalidated whenever work on the page is orphaned/deleted
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3426
Currently when a work is deleted or orphaned, the works index page cache is not invalidated

We were trying to do this manually with a cache sweeper but it has a lot of problems.


Instead, I've now reworked so the cache key itself will change (and thereby invalidate
the cached stuff) automatically whenever the contents of the page should change. 

The cache index key is now made up of:
+ The @owner type and id -- @owner is eg the tag  in .../tag/TAGNAME/works, or the
user in /users/USERNAME/works, or the collection in /collections/COLLECTIONNAME/works

+ The count of works belonging to that @owner

+ The updated_at timestamp of the most recently updated work belonging to that @owner


How this invalidates: 

* The count will capture a change in any works that were orphaned/deleted
* The most recently updated-at value will capture new works or edited works
* Can't orphan/delete and keep the count the same except by posting a new work with
new updated_at

In addition, the redis queue will touch now works when they get reindexed because of
wrangling changes, which will un-stale their filters; that will be on the 7min delay
but that seems reasonable. 

See the revised index_cache_key method in works_controller.

all the series a work is in with little "x"s next to them for removal _upon posting_.
