column1: Revamp em scale, increase line height, make skin of old values
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3462*

*What archive revision are you testing on? (See the version label in the footer, for example v0.8.13.8.)*

0.9.4.2

*If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:*

Any

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*

# Set your browser font size 
# Expect the main text of the Archive to respect that

*What is the expected output? What do you see instead?*

If I set my browser font size to 12px, I expect the majority of the Archive's text to be 12px. Instead, it is in 10.5px because our main text is set to 0.875em (0.875 x 12 = 10.5). Work text is 11.3px instead of 12px because the work font size is set to 1.08em (0.875 x 1.08 x 12 = 11.3). The default font size setting of most browsers is 16px, so most users see the majority of our text at 14px (0.875 x 16 = 14).

While some browsers will let me set a minimum font size, this is less than ideal if I want the font to be larger: just because I want to see most text in 24px doesn't mean I want to force the date on work blurbs to be 24px as well.

Additionally, 0.875em is not a pleasant number for coders to work with. Check out our
front end documentation and compare the numbers from [The Scale in Ems to the numbers from Our Em Scale|http://otwcode.github.com/docs/front_end_coding/em-scale.html ].

We end up using awkward numbers that we have to round to the nearest thousandth, and sometimes browsers differ in the way they round numbers. For instance, we frequently use 0.25em.

0.25 x 14 = 3.5. 

Opera rounds this down to 3px while Safari rounds it up to 4px.

We currently use 1.286 to set our line height to 18px for most users (1.286 x 14 = 18). We use unitless line height, not ems, but it is the same principle and needs to be adjusted along with the rest of the scale. However, instead of just changing it to 1.125 to keep lines at roughly 18px, we will increase it to 1.5 in order to meet the [Web Content Accessibility Guidelines|http://www.w3.org/TR/2008/WD-WCAG20-TECHS-20080430/C21.html].

I'm also copying the old numbers into a skin so Support can direct any unhappy users that way. (Alternatively, they could decrease their browser's default font size and rarely have to see size 16 body text anywhere on the web...)

NOTE: Please do mention if you notice issues with:

* inconsistency with other things on the archive
* how this might work for screenreader/mobile/other devices or users with other accessibility issues
* overlap with other features or gap left between features
* the clarity and conciseness of the text
* how well one action flows to another
* how intuitive you find the correct actions
* if not intuitive, how badly things go wrong if you do what you find intuitive

1. Log in
2. Go to my home
3. Go to Preferences
4. Set Your time zone to something
5. Find a work with no comments
6. Leave a comment on that work
7. Notice that the time zone reflects the time zone you set
8. Go to my home

their own user preferences. Instead, we have the timestamp inside the memcached portion
of the comment, which means users see the timestamp displayed in the time zone the
first commenter had set when they left the comment.

What archive revision are you testing on?* 0.9.4.2 Beta, 0.9.5.0 Test

http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/works/search?utf8=✓&work_search%5Bquery%5D=samjohnsson&commit=Search
(works as of 2013 01 10)

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*
1. Create an account with UserNameA
2. Post works, making note of at least one canonical tag you use.
3. Change user name to UserNameB. For ease of testing, the new user name should start with a letter from a very different part of the alphabet (e.g. UserNameA should be Alpha and UserNameB should be Zeta).

For the work search version:
4. Search > Works
5. Enter UserNameA in the "Any Field" field
6. Press "Search"

The results will show all posted works from step 2, though the blurb lists UserNameB

For the work listings version:
4. Go to the work listing for the tag from step 2
5. In the filters, select "Author" from "Sort by"
6. Press "Sort and Filter"

If you look through the listings, you'll see the works from step 2 are all sorted alphabetically by UserNameA, not UserNameB. The blurbs will show UserNameB.

In either case, this can violate user identity safety.

Initially reported by user in https://otw.16bugs.com/projects/4911/bugs/248642, confirmed by me.

Elz notes: 
the pseud showing up in people search has an icon attributed to the other user's old username

column1: Duplicate and invalid Collections can be created by submitting the form twice very fast
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3475
What archive revision are you testing on? otwarchive v0.9.4.2

What steps will reproduce the problem?
Fill a New Collection form, and submit it twice very fast.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

The second submitting should be rejected. Instead, duplicate collections are created.
Because they're duplicate, they are invalid. Uniqueness needs to be enforced at the
database level.

Reported here: [https://otw.16bugs.com/projects/4911/bugs/248568|https://otw.16bugs.com/projects/4911/bugs/248568]

Note that in order to add a uniqueness constraint at the database level, we first need to handle any pre-existing collections with duplicate names. Otherwise the migration won’t run (if it’s a standard migration) or it will remove duplicates (if it’s a {{pt-osc}} migration).

As in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5923|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5923|smart-link], a PR for this issue should probably include the following:

* A rake task to rename duplicate collections (e.g. “Collection” => “Collection_2”).
* A migration to add the uniqueness constraint. 

h2. Deploy notes

For the Staging deploy please follow the testing instructions.

For the production deploy:

After deploying, run the rake task: {{bundle exec rake After:rename_duplicate_collections}} 

*After* that task has been run successfully, run the migration (with departure): {{rails db:migrate:up VERSION=20260728014110}}

h2. Testing instructions

This needs to be tested by a database admin and can only be tested once as part of the deploy to Staging

column27:

What archive revision are you testing on? (See the version label in

v0.9.5.13

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Click the "Mark for Later" button to mark a work for later or the "Mark as read"
button to mark a work as read
2. Get a flash message saying the work has been added to your Marked for Later list
(in both cases--see Issue 3501), but note that the button is still on the work
3. Click the button again, just to be sure

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

Expect your work to be marked for later and added to your Marked for Later list, or
marked as read and removed from your Marked for Later list.  Instead see that it doesn't
appear or go away as expected.

Please use labels and text to provide additional information.

The buttons are behaving like toggles.  Clicking once will lead to the work being properly
marked, twice won't, three times will.

There is a significant delay (~10 minutes) for a work to recognize that it has been
either marked for later or marked as read.  In the meantime, the button is still there
and clickable.  In the latter case, the fact that the flash message when marking as
read says you're marking for later (Issue 3501) compounds the confusion, and makes
it more likely a user will click twice.

Related ticket:  https://otw.16bugs.com/projects/4911/bugs/249771

column127:
13/Jun/20 11:57 AM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;When you use {{ChaptersController#post}} to post the first chapter of a multichapter draft, the sequence of code is, roughly:

{noformat}@chapter.posted = true
@chapter.save
@work.save
@work.update_attribute(:posted, true) unless @work.posted?{noformat}

After the first two lines, {{@chapter.posted}} is true, and that value has been saved to the database.

The third line is where things get weird. The work model has this callback, intended to post the first chapter when the work changes from unposted to posted:

{noformat}  # If the work is posted, the first chapter should be posted too
  def post_first_chapter
    chapter_one = self.first_chapter
    if self.saved_change_to_posted? || (chapter_one && chapter_one.posted != self.posted)
      chapter_one.published_at = Date.today unless self.backdate
      chapter_one.posted = self.posted
      chapter_one.save
    end
  end{noformat}

[(Source)|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/6ce960255567efa9550046db4c70fc37f5e80992/app/models/work.rb#L641-L649]

At this point, however, the work is still unposted, but the chapter is posted. So {{chapter_one.posted != self.posted}}, and the code inside the {{if}} block will run, setting {{chapter_one.posted}} to false and saving. This means that in an attempt to post the chapter, the work callback ends up _unposting_ the chapter (temporarily).

The last of the four lines fixes this, because the work is unposted. The same {{post_first_chapter}} callback ends up reposting the first chapter again.

However, the {{set_word_count}} callback runs before the {{post_first_chapter}} callback. This means that it correctly calculates the word count the first time the work is saved (because the chapter was set to posted before the callback), but incorrectly calculates the word count the second time the work is saved (because the chapter is still unposted when the callback runs).

The result is a {{nil}} word count. I’m not sure why the word count would spontaneously fix itself after a few minutes, though. (Presumably something else calls {{save}} or {{update}} on the work again?)

column1: Dynamically added forms contain elements with duplicate ids
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3512
What archive revision are you testing on? (See the version label in
the footer, for example v0.95)

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:
(list is probably not exhaustive!)
/bookmarks
/collections/$SOME_COLLECTION/signups/new

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Visit a page which gets multiple copies of the same kind of form added dynamically.
2. Initiate the action to add a form (eg: save a bookmark from bookmarks index; "add
another request" on collection signup page) to the page. Do it multiple times so multiple
forms are added.
3. Inspect the elements inside the forms.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?
Ids on all elements on the page should be unique. Instead, multiple elements with the
same id get added to the page. This is not inherently problematic; however it is invalid
HTML, and it invites JS grief.

Please use labels and text to provide additional information.
Options for resolving include 
1) Append the data object id to form element ids to create multiple unique ids, eg:
"bookmark_notes_24583" as opposed to multiple instances of "bookmark_notes". Comments
forms currently use this approach; bookmarks forms on index pages will use this approach
as of 0.96.
2) Don't use the DOM id attribute; put the data object id in an attribute like "data-id",
if it even needs to be stored in the DOM at all.

column1: Comment threads squished on narrow displays
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3528
What archive revision are you testing on? 0.95

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:
Any page with threaded comments, like a work chapter or a news post.

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Expand the comments section.
2. Make or find a series of replies 3+ levels deep.  (more levels makes the problem
worse)
3. Shrink your browser window (if you're not already on a phone) to ~300px wide.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?
Comment boxes should remain wide enough to read the text inside. Instead, the indenting
for replies makes them very narrow, to the point where they can only fit one word per
line.


=== user did some investigation in their ticket, pasting below: ===

There is a comment on the “Meta” news post pointing out that comments, and in particular
long comment threads, are difficult to view on a mobile device. They are so narrow
that you can get one letter of each word stacked vertically when you have a small screen.

This is caused by two things:

The div with the ID of feedback (the one that encloses the comment form and all comments
on news and work pages) has some left and right margin space in ems. This is not overridden
on the mobile stylesheet.

Two, the indentation that visually shows the threaded nature of the comments is a left
margin of 3ems on .thread .thread.

Therefore, on a mobile device, comments on any post or work have a lot of whitespace
on each side, and that whitespace increases with larger fonts, since that’s how ems
work.

My suggestion, which I’m afraid to type out in code since your system strips so many
characters, was to add to the mobile stylesheet some code that would change that indentation
to two percent, rather than 3ems, so that the size of the indent is dependant on screen
width rather than the size of the font. Also, if you remove the right and left margin
from the div “feedback” on that stylesheet, that excess margin space goes away too.
The result is a lot more space for comments and a lot less unnecessary margin allowing
a more subtle indentation that still visually cues threading.

My initial thought was to simply make a skin to do this. The commenter also said that
on a wider screen there is a great deal of white space to the left of the comments
as well, so I thought offering users a full width comment option would be nice.

I made a skin, which has a parent that puts a negative margin on the div “feedback”
for non-mobile view, allowing it to stretch over into the space left for the dashboard
list on the left of the div ID of “main”. I then chained to that a skin that would
make my suggestions above apply on mobile view.

However, your actual mobile style sheet uses a media condition of both screen size
of less than 480 pixels and handheld. Your skin system just uses handheld as a media
type, so I don’t trust any code in it to trigger on all narrow widths and override
the code in the parent skin. Your skin system should produce media conditions that
match your base stylesheet. I could not submit my skin to be made public, or suggest
it to anyone, since any mobile device that didn’t load CSS under handheld, and there
are a bunch, would have a borked view.

column1: Batch wrangling and general overhaul of tag wrangle pages
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3531 Note: This feature requires familiarity with the wrangling interface. We want the “Wrangle” page for tags (i.e. the ao3.org/tags/TAGNAME/wrangle, such as http://archiveofourown.org/tags/Homestuck/wrangle ) overhauled to simplify the wrangling process, especially to give us batch-wrangling features so we can wrangle multiple tags at once. Currently many wrangling actions require us to open individual tag edit pages, which is very time consuming, as well as putting more load on the servers. Batch wrangling is essential if wranglers are to keep up with the volume of new tags we are seeing on the Archive now. Detailed feature description (see attached mockup) Please note: every different table should be slightly different, featuring different columns and different batch-wrangle actions. The mockup is an example "All" page for Characters. General changes: 1. "edit tag and parent associations" button text changed to "edit [TAGTYPE] tag & associations" to make use clearer 2. Text change "showing [TYPE] [TAGTYPE]" to "showing [TYPE] [TAGTYPE] tags" to be clearer (e.g. "showing canonical characters" changed to "showing canonical character tags") 3. "Add new characters" removed from page (function is still available from the above-linked page) 4. "Batch-wrangle tags" section added, with various actions listed to be applied to all selected tags: Mark as Canonical, Mark as Unwrangleable, Remove from This [TAGTYPE], and Wrangle to Fandom with a selection box (allowing us to mass-add the tags of one fandom to another fandom, such as moving Marvel chars to new movie fandoms) All of these actions, if applied to a tag that is already canonical or unwrangleable, should just be skipped without an error message 5. "Wrangle" buttons removed (as now superfluous) 6. Changes to mass-wrangle table: * Canonical & Synonym columns merged (saves room and is easier to read & understand; making tags canonical now a batch-wrangling feature) * Batch-wrangling checkbox column added (with all/none selection buttons) * Tag comments column added, showing comment count if >0 linking to comments; or else added "comments" button in "Manage" column * "Remove" button removed from the "Manage" column (moved to batch wrangling) * "wrangle" button removed from "Manage" column(except possibly on the "Mergers" page for fandoms/make the "wrangle" page otherwise accessible?) Batch-wrangling features on specific pages: * Viewing tags: "All" ** Batch-wrangling: Mark as Canonical, Mark as Unwrangleable, Remove from This [TAGTYPE], and Wrangle to Fandom with a selection box * Viewing tags: "Canonical" ** Batch-wrangling: Remove from this fandom, wrangle to another fandom ** "Canonical" column removed (superfluous!) * Viewing tags: "Non-canonical" ** Should be changed to "Synonyms" as per previous request, and show only synonyms ** Batch-wrangling: Remove from this fandom, wrangle to another fandom ** ("Canonical" column renamed to "Synonym to"? Not required; keeping it Canonical/Synonyms is fine) * Viewing tags: "Unfilterable" ** Batch-wrangling: Mark as canonical, Mark as Unwrangleable, Remove from this fandom, Wrangle to another fandom * Viewing tags: "Unfilterable" ** Batch-wrangling: Mark as canonical, Mark as Unwrangleable, Remove from this fandom, Wrangle to another fandom ** "Canonical" column removed (superfluous!) * Viewing tags: "Unwrangled" (moved to last position, as makes more sense???) ** Batch-wrangling: Add to this fandom (will add all checked tags to whatever fandom you are wrangling in, without having to enter the fandom name into the box), Wrangle to another fandom (to easily dispose of No Fandom tags!) ** Canonical/Synonym column should remain, as occasionally canonical tags do end up unwrangled by mistake and it's good to be able to see these! * Viewing tags: "Unwrangleable" ** Batch-wrangling: Mark as wrangleable (the only feature, as unwrangleable tags should be marked as wrangleable before we do anything else with them, else they risk getting lost...) The same features should be available on the Characters and Freeforms lists. Batch-wrangling features are probably not necessary on other tags with children (Characters, Media) other than "remove from this tag" (which can be left as a separate check button if that's easier; training-wise it would be preferable to have them have the batch-wrangling feature as well, but only have "remove from this tag") (copied from https://transformativeworks.basecamphq.com/W5232636 )

column1: Allow non-canonical child tags to be added from tag wrangle and edit pages

column27:

Currently the system only allows us to add canonical children tags from the fandom pages
(e.g. on  http://archiveofourown.org/tags/Homestuck/wrangle or http://archiveofourown.org/tags/Homestuck/edit
where it says "add characters/relationships/freeforms", the autocomplete only brings
up canonical tags, and only lets us add those.)

However, non-canonical tags *can* be added as children from the mass-wrangle bins and
on the edit pages for the child tags.

The "Add new tags" fields on these pages:
archiveofourown.org/tags/TAGNAME/wrangle
archiveofourown.org/tags/TAGNAME/edit

should allow non-canonical tags to be entered and added.

Ideally the autocomplete for these fields should pull from both canonical and non-canonical
tags; however if that's unfeasible, it would be all right if non-canonical tags had
to be entered manually.

To test for:

If a non-existent tag is entered into these fields, it should degrade gracefully and
not error.

Tags from other categories should not be able to be added (so the Add characters should
only allow Character tags to be added, not Relationships, Freeforms, or Fandoms.)

05/Nov/15 7:43 PM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;Here is the final summary of current behavior: 

* I can turn on comment moderation per work either when posting new or editing an existing work. 
* I can also turn on/off comment moderation and anonymous commenting for multiple works at once from the Edit Works page (link on dashboard). 
* Existing comments will NOT go into moderation. Any new comments posted whether by anonymous or Archive users will go into moderation. The author's own comments do not go into moderation. 
* There should be appropriate notices on the comment form and when posting to let users know that their comment is being moderated and will not appear publicly. Emails should similarly have appropriate notices and also links to approve comments for the owner of the work. 
* The user can edit or delete their own unmoderated comment. If they have javascript enabled, the comment will appear on the page for them and can be edited/deleted from there. They can also reach it from the "thread starting from this comment" link in their email notification if they are being notified of their own comments.
* The author will see a button "Unreviewed Comments" on their moderated work. This page should list all the unreviewed comments, paginated, in flat order (not threaded). Each comment can be approved or deleted individually, and there is an "Approve All" button which should approve all the existing comments on the work at once. 
* The author should also see unreviewed comments listed in their inbox and the homepage. They should be able to Approve the comments. They should not be able to reply to unreviewed comments. 
* Once comments are approved, they should appear in the comments listing normally. 
* If a comment is edited significantly then it will be put back into moderation. ("Significantly" will vary -- the current maximum is 10 letters changed, but if more than one letter in a row is changed, it will make the changes more likely to get put back into moderation, so for testing this, the best plan is to mostly try fixing small typos or just inserting an apostrophe if you want to keep a work out of moderation, or adding 11 letters at the end if you want to get it put back in.)
* When a threaded comment is approved, the owner of the comment it was replying to should be notified (not before). 
* If comment moderation is turned off, the unreviewed comments will remain unapproved. The work owner should still be able to view unreviewed comments and approve them all. 

WHEW

14/Jun/21 7:19 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;I think this is a bug in the code intended to fix unclosed tags, e.g. when you typo: {noformat}Emphasized. Not emphasized.{noformat} Unfortunately, there are a few issues with this code: * The code to fix unclosed tags runs after the sanitizer, which parses the HTML. This results in all of the missing closing tags being added. So by the time the data gets to {{add_paragraphs_to_text}}, which is the part of the code that tries to fix unclosed tags, there are no “real” unclosed tags left to fix. * The sanitizer outputs HTML, not XML. This means that for self-closing tags like {{br}} and {{img}} (see also [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3313|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3313|smart-link]), it won’t include the final {{/}} indicating to the XML parser that the tag is self-closing. This in turn means that when the code is passed to the XML parser, it views {{
}} and {{}} as unclosed tags, and tries to close them. * Finally, it seems like the code for fixing unclosed tags doesn’t work properly. This is the set of errors that Nokogiri gives in cases like these: {noformat} > puts Nokogiri::XML.parse("hello
goodbye").errors 1:39: FATAL: Opening and ending tag mismatch: br line 1 and em 1:48: FATAL: Opening and ending tag mismatch: em line 1 and myroot 1:48: FATAL: Premature end of data in tag myroot line 1{noformat} The method for fixing unclosed tags looks for tags that have a mismatch with {{myroot}}, so while the parser does flag an error about {{
}}, that’s not the tag it tries to close. Instead, it tries to close the {{}}, which already has a closing tag and probably doesn’t need another one. As a result, the {{}} tag is closed right before the {{
}}, and doesn’t extend to the next line. (And in the case of AO3-3313, the {{}} tag is closed right before the {{}} tag starts.) (My inclination would be to remove the code for fixing unclosed tags. It doesn’t seem like we’re getting enough information from Nokogiri to fix the unclosed tag in all cases. And it’s not like we’d be removing functionality, because {{Sanitize}} runs before {{add_paragraphs_to_text}}.)

clicking the Comments (#) link on the bottom of the page when Javascript is enabled

appear. Do not use the Comments link on the top of the work, since that does not load

column1: Feeds and downloads don't update
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3583
There is an assumption that feeds and downloads are stored on shared storage.

This is an issue with the feeds as they are all in a single directory and there are
too many for the nas to have that many directories in a directory.

The right answer is to have a resque or rabbitmq queue so that when a feed needs updating
it will place a task on the queue and the first web server picks up the task an deletes
its copy ( creating another task for any other web server ).


The current work around is to delete all the feeds periodically ( currently every 24
hours ), this task runs every 2 hours from cfengine.

column1: Live validation errors permanently replace form submit buttons with "Please wait..." message
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3591*

Original name was “Submitting the work post/edit form without a title and/or with too few words of work text makes the choice to Post Without Preview vanish”

*What archive revision are you testing on? (See the version label in the footer, for example v0.8.13.8.)*

v0.9.6.12-ish

*If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:*

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*

1.  Submit the work posting (or edit) form without a title and/or at least 10 words of work text, either by choosing Preview or Post

*What is the expected output? What do you see instead?*

Expect to be able to fill in the missing information and then have the option to either Preview or Post. 

*What do you see instead?*

Instead the Post button has turned into "Please wait....", so the only option for posting is now to Preview first.

*Please use labels and text to provide additional information.*

Having only the fandom and/or warnings missing gives a flash error message and does not cause the Post button to go away.

This issue was introduced as a side-effect of Issue 2757, "Add Javascript to prevent double submission of forms". (AO3-2754)

It apples to any form that uses the aforementioned JavaScript and that has LiveValidation fields that require input (or input of a certain length), including but not limited to:

* logged out comment form, when neglecting to enter a name or email
* support form, when neglecting to enter a summary or comment

[Additional note|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/3982#pullrequestreview-617094477] from Sarken regarding the solution:

{quote}I think we need to make sure the LiveValidation error is resolved before we reenable the submit button. If we don't, it's just going to do the "Please wait..." thing all over again without the user having any idea what's going on. (And if for some reason the button _isn't_ stuck in that state due to a LiveValidation error, but rather because the site or the user's connection is horrendously slow, we definitely don't want to [automatically] reenable the button [after a certain time] and let the user resubmit the form.)

I think the best thing to do is going to be scroll the user to the first field with the error, make sure it and all the other errors are resolved, and then reenable the button.{quote}

*Testing notes*

Please see if this helps with the problem in other locations that disable the submit button when the fields are not all filled in:

* comment form (logged out is the best to test)
* chapter form
* support form

column124:
08/Jun/21 12:59 AM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;Hmm. This does scroll as expected, and it does reenable the button once the errors are corrected, _but_ I think there are some accessibility issues. 

It appears as though focus remains on the “Please wait…” button, so screen reader users aren’t taken to the field with the error. They’re basically still getting the same experience: the form is just mysteriously stuck.

Unfortunately, if a field with a live validation error receives focus, the error message disappears, which is going to be confusing for everyone. (I don’t think live validation errors are currently coded in an accessible way, either – that is, I don’t think anything alerts you to their presence even if they’re visible to sighted users. However, that should be dealt with separately.) 

The easiest fix that leaps to mind is making it so the live validation error doesn’t go away until you start to enter text in the field. 

[WebAIM also has some suggestions for dealing with form errors|https://webaim.org/techniques/formvalidation/#error].
column125: 13/Jun/21 2:25 AM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;Created a new issue for improving the accessibility of the error messages themselves: [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6183|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6183|smart-link]

05/Apr/13 5:49 PM;557058:8eb04462-c6aa-4b1b-b7b4-259ed44d3c0b;That's fascinating! :D (In the "close a cupboard door, the oven starts beeping" way,
but still.)

I thought we had it (and I thought the way to do it was) so that on document.ready,
if the user has JS enabled, of course, we'd reveal any elements specifically marked
to: be hidden until javascript is proven to exist; be revealed on first loading of
the page.

And then all sorts of events get associated, and fired when something or other is clicked,
etc.

Whereas here it looks like the ways of doing it got overlapped, and an unfortunate
double toggle occurred. >.< Not sure what's the best way to solve it though, but all
the <3 to you for tackling it!
column121:
05/Apr/13 6:50 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;"I thought we had it (and I thought the way to do it was) so that on document.ready,
if the user has JS enabled, of course, we'd reveal any elements specifically marked
to: be hidden until javascript is proven to exist; be revealed on first loading of
the page."

That's the general idea of what we're doing -- locating the hidden class and removing
it -- but we don't have one single function in our application.js that covers all the
instances of hidden classes across the site. We do a lot of showing and hiding things
in a lot of different patterns (e.g. items we always want showing if the user has JavaScript
enabled, items we only want showing after the user has clicked something else) with
more than a few different class names, and were, I suspect, making a lot of stuff up
as we went along, so it got away from us before anyone said, "Hey, we should have one
standard way of doing this."

So now we have a case where we have a bunch of little bits of JavaScript scattered
throughout our partials, and, if I remember correctly, in some helpers, too. Someone
could attempt to clean it up, but I can absolutely guarantee stuff will be missed and
it will be a nasty, unpleasant project for planning, coding, and testing. It would
be lovely to have it fixed, but, well...

Anyway, what's going on here is we used the hidden class to make the Share button on
your own bookmarks hidden when JavaScript is disabled, since the Share buttons do awful
things and aren't even useful if you have JavaScript disabled. That's the $j(".actions
.hidden").removeClass("hidden"); in the bookmarks/_bookmark_owner_navigation partial.
But we also use the hidden class to toggle the Expand Fandoms List and Collapse Fandoms
List button in the user/_contents partial. When you're on your own dashboard, both
of those partials are used at once, so $j(".actions .hidden").removeClass("hidden");
latches onto the hidden class on the Expand/Collapse buttons and removes it. So we
end up with both buttons visible initially. When I click the Expand button, it does
$j("#collapse-fandoms").toggleClass("hidden");$j(this).toggleClass("hidden"); -- and
thus the hidden class is added back to *both* buttons and they go bye-bye. To fix it,
all I have to do is add the bookmarks class to make it $j(".bookmarks .actions .hidden").removeClass("hidden");
-- then it will only target hidden action items within the bookmark blurb.

THIS IS ALL MY FAULT. It was a last-minute fix for a problem with the Share boxes and
the new modals. I also added it to the Share portion of works/_work_header_navigation
and am going to tweak the targeting on that, too, just so it never causes a problem
like this there, either. And for double stupidity, I failed to take into account that
the contents of bookmarks/_bookmark_owner_navigation are rendered once per own bookmark,
so now we have pages that have <script type="text/javascript">//<![CDATA[$j(".actions
.hidden").removeClass("hidden");//]]></script> TWENTY FREAKING TIMES.

Oops, fml, etc.

Purpose of code changes:
to add a second solution to support right-to-left languages in works (even when we
resolve https://code.google.com/p/otwarchive/issues/detail?id=3541), propose we add
the following class to the Basic Formatting workskin:

.userstuff .rtl {

}

really a thing at this point, but in general, using the HTML attribute is the best
way to do this. Direction is important to the overall meaning of the document, which
makes it markup material rather than styling material. In our specific case, it's especially
important to use the attribute because we make it so easy for users to disable work
skins. Additionally, setting the direction with CSS just plain old doesn't always work,
as I found out while fixing issue 3726.

More: http://www.w3.org/International/questions/qa-bidi-css-markup

column1: Deleting a pseud and choosing "Transfer these bookmarks to the default pseud" does not update default pseud's bookmark index
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Steps to reproduce:* 

You'll need to create a pseud, use it to bookmark some works, and then delete the pseud and transfer its bookmarks to the default pseud.

1. Log in
2. Hi, username! > My Preferences > Manage My Pseuds > New Pseud
3. Fill in a pseud name, e.g. "Bookmarking Pseud"
4. Press "Create"
5. Browse > Works > [Work Title] > Bookmark
6. On the open bookmark form at the bottom of the work, select "Bookmarking Pseud" from the select menu where it says "[select menu] save a bookmark!"
7. Press "Create"
8. Repeat steps 5-7 to make as many bookmarks as desired. You might want to bookmark some works with your default pseud, too.
9. Hi, username! > My Preferences > Manage My Pseuds
10. Under "Bookmarking Pseud," choose "Delete"
11. When the confirmation pop-up appears, press "OK" to confirm
12. On the "Pseud deletion" page, choose the "Transfer these bookmarks to the default pseud" option
13. Press "Submit"

*What should happen:*

The bookmarks should appear on the default pseud's bookmark page, ideally within a few hours.

*What happens:*

The bookmarks continue to exist (e.g. if you go to the work you've bookmarked, you'll see "Edit Bookmark" rather than "Bookmark" at the top), but never show up on the default pseud's bookmark page. Someone with database access has to reindex the user's bookmarks from the console. Using the admin troubleshoot option does not appear to resolve this issue.

*Notes:* 

The original issue information follows. I have _not_ noticed a problem with the counts becoming out of sync with the number of bookmarks displayed on the page, but I wouldn't be surprised if that happened occasionally. Heck, I wouldn't be surprised if transferring bookmarks _did_ work from time to time. Indexing bugs are fun.

{quote}Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3607
What archive revision are you testing on? otwarchive v0.9.6.11

What steps will reproduce the problem?

No clue how to reproduce it. The user reported having changed their username recently,
though the words used imply deleting a pseud:

"I have changed my name recently but transferred the bookmarks to my new username"

Both things could be tried. User had 58 bookmarks when it happened.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

One would expect to see the number of public bookmarks (if one is logged in as a different
user or logged off) in between parenthesis in the Dashboard link to bookmarks:

Bookmarks (58)

That works.

On clicking, one would expect to see all public bookmarks in a paginated list, that
one can filter. 

Instead, both for the user and everyone else, the list showed only 8 bookmarks, plus
any that the user kept adding after the problem occurred (went up to 11).

Elz poked it to re-index and it now works. Says the index was out of date.

Report is here https://otw.16bugs.com/projects/4911/bugs/257755 (no extra info offered){quote}

column1: Tags that begin with a capital letter with an accent or other diacritical mark do not show up in the autocomplete if no fandom is entered
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3623

*What archive revision are you testing on?*

v0.9.6.11

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*

# Start to enter a common/canonical tag that starts with a capital letter with a diacritical
mark in a posting or search form

*What is the expected output? What do you see instead?*

Expect to see the tag show up in the autocomplete list.  Instead, do not.

These tags won't come up if you type the capital letter with the mark, the capital letter without the mark, or the lowercase letter with the mark.

If the letter with the diacritical mark is not the first letter of the tag, it won't have this problem and will properly appear.

Reported in ticket [https://otw.16bugs.com/projects/4911/bugs/259586|https://otw.16bugs.com/projects/4911/bugs/259586]

From the ticket:

{quote}"Tags that start with capital letters with diacritics or some other upper-case special characters don’t come up in tag autofill – typing the capital letter will bring up tags with words that start with the lower-case version (if any) but not tags that begin with the upper-case version; the lower-case letter doesn’t bring up tags that use the upper-case either.

Examples of tags that won’t appear in autofill: Éomer ; Çagap ; Álvaro should bring up three different Sports RPF people but doesn’t; Østenfor should bring up ‘Østenfor sol og vestenfor måne | East of the Sun and West of the Moon’ but doesn’t.

Punctuation works, as do lower-case special characters, but so far every upper-case special character I’ve tried has had this problem."{quote}

*Notes*

This bug only happens if you don’t enter a fandom.

Autocomplete data will need to be regenerated for this fix to apply to existing tags.

column119:
15/May/13 2:11 PM;557058:0670e11e-5036-4aae-af3f-d6ae02967b60;More details:

Just to clarify, because I think I was unintentionally unclear: it’s not that it’s
the first letter of the tag that’s the bug; as far as I know, the autofill doesn’t
recognize capital-letter diacritics anywhere in the tag. It’s just that with multi-word
tags, it’s usually possible to find it in autofill by typing the words in the tag that
don’t start with a capitalized diacritic.

“Dèng Ài”, for example, won’t give results if you type “Ài”, but it will if you type
“Dèng,” so it’s not as much of a usability issue there. “Éponine Thénardier” won’t
come up for “Éponine” but will for “Thénardier” That’ s why I used examples of one-word
tags: those are the cases where it’s really impossible to get the tag in autofill.
But it still fails if you try to find words that start with a capitalized diacritic
that occur anywhere in a tag. Admittedly, I haven’t found any canonical tags with a
capital-letter diacritic in the middle of a word, but I suspect it would also be an
issue there should that happen.

Lower-case diacritics: I don’t know of any where the tag itself starts with a lower-case
diacritic, but there are some where a word later in the tags starts with one: if you
type just É in the autofill, you should see ‘Communauté : obscur échange’ come up in
autofill, and À gets you several tags with the french preposition ‘à’ in a title.

Update: it does seem to work (sort of) if the name with the diacritic is the second
character in a pairing?

“Combeferre/Ép’’ brings up the correct result (Combeferre/Éponine Thénardier) as the
first option in the autofill, although “Combeferre/É” doesn’t, and I don’t understand
how the autofill sorts pairing results in the first place, so maybe it’s just ignoring
the É completely.

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. View the orphan account's profile page and press "Subscribe". Note the confirmation
of your new subscription.

3. Wait for / manually trigger batch subscription delivery.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?
I expect notification about a new work from orphan_account. Instead I get nothing.

h2. What should happen

Due to issues such as [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5696|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5696|smart-link] causing confusion for users, we'd like to resolve this by:

* removing the ability to subscribe to orphan_account. Users should receive a message saying: {{Sorry, you can't subscribe to orphan_account. The works on this account have been orphaned by their creators and will not receive new updates.}}
* creating a rake task to remove all current orphan_account user subscriptions
* removing the ability to subscribe to any works/series solely owned by orphan_account (as these will never be updated, it doesn't make sense to allow new subscriptions to them). Users should receive a message saying: {{You cannot subscribe to this [work/series] because it has been orphaned and will not receive new updates. You can bookmark it instead.}}

Orphaning a work/series should not affect existing subscriptions to that work/series. 

It should still be possible to subscribe to works or series that are co-created with another user (who could still update the work/series). 

Subscription emails should not say that orphan_account posted a new work in a series you’re subscribed to.

Subscription emails should not say that orphan_account posted a new chapter in a work you’re subscribed to (at least, not in the chapter byline; the work byline should continue to list all creators).

Subscription emails should not say that you are receiving this email because you are subscribed to orphan_account.

column1: Admin wrangler tracking sometimes is inaccurate
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3637*

*What archive revision are you testing on?* otwarchive v0.9.6.16

*If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:*
[http://archiveofourown.org/tags/Bosnia/edit]

When logged in as an admin, we can view the last wrangler to make a change to a tag in a "last updated" line at the bottom of the tag edit page.

However, sometimes this report is entirely incorrect. For instance, on the above tag, the wrangler is listed as:

{quote}Last updated by Zebra on 2013-05-30 14:10:22 \-0400

{quote}
Which is impossible, as Zebra is a retired wrangler who has not had wrangling permissions for several months before the date given.

We're not sure what causes this error \- whether the username is correct but the date is wrong, or that the update date is correct but the username is wrong. As we use wrangler tracking to find wranglers who are wrangling incorrectly, it's crucial that we have accurate tracking.

*Notes*

A tag’s last_wrangler is set using a before_save callback on the Tag. However, a tag’s updated_at can be changed without editing the tag – for example, if I wrangle a freeform into a fandom, the CommonTagging model will touch the tags, changing their updated_at date. 

Maybe the way around this is adding a new column, like edited_at, which can have its date set at the same time the last_wrangler is set. 

However, Tag Wrangling note that “we often get last updated dates of weeks or months earlier, for fandoms that are consistently busy,” so there is probably another issue at play that causes a tag’s updated_at not to change when CommonTaggings change.

05/Jul/19 10:38 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;I’ve been poking around, and I doubt I’ve found everything that causes this, but I think I might know one potential cause. Oddly enough, it’s linked to AO3-3631.

When a new {{CommonTagging}} is created – such as when a relationship has a new fandom added – the autocomplete for the child tag needs to be updated, so that e.g. the relationship is listed in its parent’s fandom. This works fine if the new parent is added while editing the child tag, because editing the child causes the child’s autocomplete info to be updated.

This also works if the new parent-child relationship is added while editing the parent, though it initially looks like it shouldn’t. Adding a new {{CommonTagging}} always touches the child tag, but this doesn’t trigger the autocomplete update. However, adding a new {{CommonTagging}} while {{User.current_user}} is set does trigger an update to the autocomplete. This is thanks to a callback in {{CommonTagging}} that tries to keep track of the last wrangler, and updates the autocomplete as a (possibly unintended, but useful) consequence. Hence the connection to AO3-3631.

But there are some cases where {{CommonTaggings}} can be added when {{User.current_user}} is not set, which doesn’t update the autocomplete. For example, the {{Tag#add_merger_associations}} function is called asynchronously, and I believe that Resque doesn’t set {{User.current_user}} for asynchronous wrangling jobs (which causes some of the failures in wrangler tracking). This means that any {{CommonTaggings}} added as a result of synning two tags may not be picked up by the autocomplete.

I think you should be able to replicate this bug with these steps:

# Log in as a tag wrangler.
# Create two canonical fandom tags: Canon X and Canon Y.
# Create two relationship tags: Ship A and Ship B.
# Edit Ship A and add it to Canon X.
# Edit Ship B to make it canonical and add it to Canon Y.
# Check the autocomplete on the New Work form by entering “Canon X” for the fandom, and then try typing a space in the relationships field to trigger the autocomplete. It should say “(No suggestions found)”.
# Edit Ship A and add Ship B as its synonym.
# View Ship B and note that Canon X has been added as one of its parents.
# Check the autocomplete on the New Work form by entering “Canon X” for the fandom, and then typing a space in the relationships field. It ought to list “Ship B” as a suggestion, but it doesn’t. (Make sure you open a new copy of the New Work form, since I think the results can be cached.)
# Edit Ship B and press “Save changes” without making any changes, to fix the autocomplete.
# Notice that Ship B now shows up in the autocomplete for Canon X.

(Unfortunately, I’m not sure this can be replicated in automated tests, because the async calls are performed synchronously in the same thread in the test environment. This means that {{User.current_user}} is always set properly, and so the autocomplete is always updated.)

There might be a similar way to break all relationships in a fandom by synning one canonical fandom (with children) to another. And I’m not sure why the autocomplete might be broken for a fandom that hasn’t had any recent synning. But I think this might contribute to some autocomplete issues.

We do a lot of class="<%= cycle("odd", "even") %>" to add even or odd classes to items

pages don't do anything with these classes.) Once upon a time, this was necessary.

colors on those pages (and anything else we might want to apply to even/odd elements)
with CSS. 

IE8 is the only browser we support where a pure CSS solution won't work, but alternating
background colors are hardly a major feature, although it *is* possible to add even/odd
classes via jQuery, much like we added a last class for Issue 2689.

In 10-types-groups.css, we have: a.tag, .tags a { color: #111; line-height: 1.5; text-decoration: none; padding: 0 0.125em; border-bottom: 1px dotted; } That .tags a bit means that any link inside any element with the tags class will have that style. We don't actually want that: there are quite a few places it would be useful to be able to apply the tags class without restyling all links. Like, for instance, the fandoms and metatags listboxes on that page. Or fieldset labeled Tags on the Post New form. Or some tables I was working on. Most tags links are generated with a helper that adds the class "tag" to the link itself, e.g. all the trolls. It's probably best to remove .tags a and fix the places where links to tags don't have the proper class. This would be a time consuming pain in the ass because there are 544 occurrences of the word "tags" in 144 view files. However, since I love you, I went through said occurrences... Definitely need :class => "tag" added to link_to: views/admin_posts/index.html.erb views/admin_posts/show.html.erb Might need :class => "tag" added to link_to, but I don't actually know what pages these are and can't check: views/fandoms/show.html.erb views/static/fandoms/index.html.erb views/static/fandoms/show.html.erb views/static/restricted_works/index.html.erb Iffy: views/works/_meta.html.erb -> the "Archive Warning" label in work meta links to the TOS and is not in and of itself a tag; it will be a bolded and underlined link without the tag class in the anchor, which should be fine NOTE: Please do mention if you notice issues with: - inconsistency with other things on the archive - how this might work for screenreader/mobile/other devices or users with other accessibility issues - overlap with other features or gap left between features - the clarity and conciseness of the text - how well one action flows to another - how intuitive you find the correct actions - if not intuitive, how badly things go wrong if you do what you find intuitive Please use labels and text to provide additional information.

column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3646
What archive revision are you testing on? (See the version label in
the footer, for example v0.8.13.8.)
otwarchive v0.9.6.16

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:

What steps will reproduce the problem?
0. Be an Open Doors staffer with admin powers
1. Manage the aftermath of a mass import 
2. Need to delete some duplicate works, e.g. by user request

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?
The user gets an email that reads "Your story has been deleted by our Abuse team" and
panics a bit. It should ideally say "by our Open Doors team", in such a case. 

In issue 3455 we introduced a new kind of deletion notification, primarily with Abuse
cases in mind - before that, deletion by Abuse would only deliver the usual "your work
was deleted by you" notification, confusing users. However, now it only checks if the
deleter is logged in as an admin (cf. app/models/work_observer.rb).

We need to expand on the use case of admin deletions and do one of the following: 

- create a general "by an admin" template
- hook it into the admin role architecture started in issue 3064
- make sure it correctly reflects who deleted what in some other way

column121:
26/Aug/13 10:12 AM;557058:c714f0f0-b42d-45c7-be2f-d002135599e4;So ultimately, it turned out that this wasn't a problem with the code, but with the
way the test server is set up: on production, we use a shared NAS box to store the
signup summaries, so that they can be generated by one machine and accessed by another.
On test, they're being written to the front-end server and can't be accessed by the
app server, which is why the summary never appears. The goal is ultimately to reduce
our dependency on the NAS, so we'll have to rethink how the whole system works, but
for now, it should continue to work on production, and I'd no longer call this deploy
blocking.

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. While logged out, go to the home page
2. Select "Get an invite"
3. Enter your e-mail address in the Email field (If you already have an account, try
adding something like +dontinviteme before the @whatever.com part of your e-mail.)
4. Select "Add me to the list"
5. For "Wondering how long you'll have to wait?" enter the same e-mail address you
just used
6. Select "Go"
7. Notice that the length of the queue is listed twice -- once in the paragraph under
the "Request an invite heading" and once in the paragraph under the "Invitation Status
for youremailaddress@whatever.com" heading

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?
These numbers should make sense. They don't always. That is, a Tumblr user reports
seeing "There are currently 444 people on the waiting list."" and "You are currently
number 628 on our waiting list!" How can I be 628 out of 444?

The paragraph for "Request an invite" comes from views/invite_requests/index.html.erb,
which gets the number with <%= InviteRequest.count %>. The paragraph for "Invitation
status for youremailaddress@whatever.com" comes from views/invite_requests/_invite_request.html.erb,
which gets the number with <%= invite_request.position %>.

I was able to make them not match by, after following the above steps, doing the following:
- Log in
- Select "My Dashboard" from the "Hi, username!" menu
- Selecting "Invitations"
- Selecting "Request more"
- Entering "5" for "How many invites would you like?"
- Entering a reason for "Please specify why you'd like them?"
- Selecting "Send Request"
- Selecting Log Out
- Going to the home page
- Selecting "Get an invite"
- Following steps 5-6 from the above

I cannot guarantee that this will always reproduce the bug, but I saw "There are currently
0 people on the waiting list." and "You are currently number 1 on our waiting list!"
after this. I'd expect to be number 1 of 1 people.

column121:
05/Sep/14 9:40 AM;557058:0670e11e-5036-4aae-af3f-d6ae02967b60;That's interesting.  According to Support's knowledge base, hits are intentionally not
supposed to be counted for moving between chapters, presumably as an attempt not to
have hits multiply when a single user browses a work.  (A side effect of this is that
the number of hits/chapter of a multi-chapter work will vary a lot depending on if
the work was posted in a short time (so many people experienced it all at once) or
over a period (so most people make a separate visit for each chapter).)

However, if we're achieving this by only counting hits to the first chapter, presumably
this means we entirely miss hits from users who jump straight to a later chapter (from
a subscription link, for example).  A spot test seems to indicate this may be true.

Maybe there's a better way to measure "one hit per visitor per some time period"? 
I wouldn't advocate suddenly changing it so that each visit to a chapter registers
a hit because it would make new and old multi-chapter works have radically different
results.

If you had other works on the imported archive under an e-mail address you can no longer access, please contact Open Doors with any information that can help verify your identity. column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3719
What archive revision are you testing on?  otwarchive v0.9.7.10

example: http://archiveofourown.org/works/149319

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Find a work, try to find out its language

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

Language metadata is nowhere to be found on a work. It's not in its blurb, it's not
in its header. You can't find it except by taking a stab at it and filtering by the
language you think it's marked as.

Having the information visible would help users correct mistakes with them (even to
realize they have made one), and make it easier for browsing people who aren't using
the language filters.

Visibilizing languages would also help people realize they _can_ post in other languages,
and mark the language of their works by other manners than freeform tags.

14. Notice that the most recent bookmarks are not inserted in that bookmark blurb,

Tag wranglers are currently asked not to fandom-assign tags not in their own fandoms
which are less than a month old (giving the fandom's wranglers first crack at them).
To make this rule clearer and easier to do, we want to change the default sort order
of the mass wrangle bins (these):

http://archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings?show=characters
http://archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings?show=relationships
http://archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings?show=freeforms

Currently the default sort is alphabetical; we want it to sort by date, ascending,
e.g.:

http://archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings?show=freeforms&sort_column=created_at&sort_direction=ASC

(if changing the default sort order is complicated, it would also be fine if the wrangling
sidebar's links simply pointed to the above sort order, rather than the default page.)

Note: the Fandoms bin: http://archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings?show=fandoms sort
order doesn't need to be changed (but can be, if it's simpler to change all of them.)

The default order for individual tag wrangle page such as fandom wrangle pages shouldn't
be altered.

25/Jan/15 12:34 AM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;With warnings, this definitely happens when importing a work. If "Warning:" appears
on the imported work, anything after that will be turned into a warning tag, e.g. "Warning:
F/F Smut" will lead to a new warning tag "F/F Smut" being created. There are currently
quite a few (i.e. over 100) non-canonical warnings on the Archive.

There are currently 2 non-canonical category tags. One was created in January 2013
and another was created in March 2012. It is not currently possible to create a non-canonical
category tag when importing -- story_parser.rb does not look for a "Category:" label.
Including "Category: Something" will not result in the "Something" tag being created.
The existing non-canonical category tags are "M/F - Category" and "М/М" -- note that
the latter is _not_ "M/M," but rather a Cyrillic character: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Em_(Cyrillic)

There are currently 0 non-canonical rating tags. It is not currently possible to create
non-canonical rating tags when importing. If "Rating:" exists on a work, story_parser.rb
will attempt to convert the given rating into a canonical Archive rating. If it cannot,
it will use Not Rated.- **Labels added**: Roadmap-WorkImporting

Oh, god, really?
1. Log in
2. From the Browse drop down, select Collections
3. Select New Collection
4. Enter a Collection Name, Display Title, and set "Type of challenge, if any" to Gift
Exchange
5. Submit
6. On the Gift Exchange Settings, check "Sign-up open?"

8. Select Sign-up Form from the collection dashboard side bar
9. Enter a fandom for your Request
10. Enter a fandom for your Offer
11. Submit
12. Hassle four or more friends into repeating steps 8-11
13. Wait a couple hours from the last friend's sign-up and then select Sign-up Summary
from the collection dashboard side bar

I expect to see a shiny table. I do not -- regardless of how much time has passed,
I continue to see "The summary is being generated. Please try again in a few minutes."

Please use labels and text to provide additional information.

Elz sez:

So ultimately, it turned out that this wasn't a problem with the code, but with the
way the test server is set up: on production, we use a shared NAS box to store the
signup summaries, so that they can be generated by one machine and accessed by another.
On test, they're being written to the front-end server and can't be accessed by the
app server, which is why the summary never appears. The goal is ultimately to reduce
our dependency on the NAS, so we'll have to rethink how the whole system works, but
for now, it should continue to work on production, and I'd no longer call this deploy
blocking.

column130:
27/Jan/15 1:47 PM;557058:8eb04462-c6aa-4b1b-b7b4-259ed44d3c0b;Ahhh, I've looked into it and realised what's the matter: emailing is by default asynchronous,
and this means that any parameters given to the mailer are serialised - basically,
squashed into simple data types like numbers or strings.

So the "user" that you gave as a param is no longer an ActiveRecord instance, but has
become a hash of attributes, which is what the error is saying. But the mailer method
is expecting instances, because it was copied from emails that are sent synchronously.

You have two paths before you: the quick one, and the right one. :D

Quick:
In user_creations_controller, instead of
UserMailer.admin_hidden_work_notification(creation, user).deliver
call
UserMailer.admin_hidden_work_notification(creation, user).deliver!

The bang at the end makes it synchronous - it doesn't get serialised and enqueued,
it doesn't get squashed, the user is still an ActiveRecord instance of a user and responds
to .email

Righteous:
Change the admin_hidden_work_notification method to receive and use IDs instead of
instances (creation_id, user_id, etc.)

The choice is yours, young Padawan. ;-)

column1: Specify media type for new fandom tags created in the context of tag sets
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3752
Issue: when new fandoms are added to a tag set, they are added as "Uncategorized Fandoms"
and must be wrangled before they get slotted into correct media categories, often under
time pressure given that tag sets are used for challenges. 

The tag set moderator or tag nominator should be able to specify the media category
for a new tag being added so wranglers do not have to wrangle the tags in order to
have them appear in the right category within the challenge. 


*** A design decision is required between the following two options: ***

1) Have the new tag be wrangled into the specified media category. 

2) Have the tag be associated with the specified media category only within the tag
set. Wranglers will still have to wrangle the tag into the given category officially.



The effect for the tag set will be the same. For the wranglers, #1 means less work,
#2 means more oversight. 

I'd lean towards #1 because the category selection is limited (people cannot add new
media types, they have to choose from a pull-down to specify) and the person adding
the tag is presumably as much an authority on it as we could expect to get, especially
since they know better than we do whether they mean the movie or the book version of
whatever fandom they're adding etc. So I don't see a huge advantage to taking on the
extra work. 

But either option can work fine to at least remove the time pressure from the wrangling.
column119:
22/Sep/13 10:36 AM;557058:56c6aaf0-abec-4140-88a3-59aa2f24c990;Wrangling staff discussed this and would prefer option 2 - Have the tag be associated
with the specified media category only within the tag set. Wranglers will still have
to wrangle the tag into the given category officially.

(The main reasons for preferring option 2 is that fandoms with assigned media "get
lost" in the media bins; they'll get attended to quicker if they appear in the main
fandom bin.  As well, many fandom tags are potentially cross-media or ambiguous, so
would need to have other media added anyway when they're on the archive proper.  Also
we have a ton of problems with overlapping tag set and wrangling code - wranglers "screwing
up" tag sets by wrangling tags while they're in a tag set - so the more separation
between them the better.)

However, if option 1 is substantially easier to code we can work with it!

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3754
otwarchive v0.9.8.11

1. In a tag set accepting nominations, nominate a tag like Foo [Bar]. This is a valid
tag. 

2. Review nominations. Attempt to either approve or reject the tag. The error message
will appear: "Couldn't find a fandom nomination for Foo." (or "character nomination"
etc depending on what was nominated.

fix for this is to replace the brackets in the form field names with "LBRACKET" and
"RBRACKET" and change them back afterwards in the controller.

column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3756
What archive revision are you testing on? (See the version label in
the footer, for example v0.8.13.8.)

v0.9.8.11

h2. What steps will reproduce the problem?

# Go to [http://archiveofourown.org/collections|http://archiveofourown.org/collections]
# Start to enter the name of a child collection into the "Filter by title"
box
# Choose the title of the child collection from the Autocomplete list
# Press "Sort and Filter"

h2. What happens?

You get only top level collections that share some part of the child's name.

h2. What should happen? 

Expect to get the child collection you searched for. 



Often, the parent collection does share some part of the name (CollectionName Gift
Exchange vs. CollectionName Gift Exchange 2013, for example), but if this is not the
case there is effectively no way to search or filter for the child collection.

This is the actual cause of the problem reported in Issue 2803.  (Kaleidoscope is a
sub-collection of Dark Agenda)

h2. Steps to reproduce

Scenario 1:

# Log in
# Post > New Work
# Fill in the required fields

# Note that there is a flash message at the top saying “Your changes have not been saved. Please post your work or save the draft if you want to keep them.”

# Log in

# Follow the content policy link

In both scenarios the flash message stays around, even though you’re no longer viewing a work or chapter preview.

h2. What should happen

The flash message should go away once you leave the work/chapter page.

h2. Development notes

Because the update action in the works controller and the chapter controller {{render}} the preview they shoulder use {{flash.now}} instead of the plain {{flash}} which stays around through an extra page.

column1: Tag Set view cache is not expired when a tag in a Tag Set is wrangled
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3765
What archive revision are you testing on? (See the version label in
the footer, for example v0.8.13.8.)

v0.9.8.11

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*
1. Create a tag set with Supernatural and Dean, Teen Wolf and Derek. (Dean should automatically
be listed under SPN, Derek under TW.)
2. Wrangle Derek into Supernatural. 
3. Look at the tag set again.

*What is the expected output? What do you see instead?*

Expect to see Derek listed under Supernatural.  Instead, do not.

Please use labels and text to provide additional information.

Editing the Tag Set and Updating will make the changes appear.

From Shalott:

When a tag is canonically wrangled (typically a fandom added or removed) the changes
are not reflected in any tag sets where that tag appears. This happens because the
tag set view cache isn't expired after wrangling. 

Probably the right fix for this is to add some code to the tag_sweeper to go through
any owned tag sets where the tag appears, and expire the tag set view cache there.
(See tag_set_sweeper for the way to expire the tag set view cache.)

column129:
20/Sep/14 2:24 AM;557058:563cc0f0-cad4-465b-b3f4-47e1e66c2d4a;Did the following successfully:

- Create a new FAQ category (defaults to English) by putting in Category title and
two question & answer pairs plus page anchors, then hitting Post.
- The new category will show up on the main FAQ index, and expanding/collapsing all
questions works beautifully (have to test in more browsers when FAQs have been posted).
- Category page has table of contents at the top, with anchor links to each question.
- This all also works on the iPhone.

SO MUCH AWESOME!! \o/



Translation process as I understand it:

- To translate a FAQ, load up the index in admin mode, pick a language from the drop-down,
then open a category to edit. The URL for this editing process will have the selected
locale in it, telling the system to save the category in this language.
- Overwrite the English content you see with the language in question (leaving the
anchors alone) and make sure to change/translate the category title as well.
- Posting will create the translated FAQ.
- Note that the admin index in any language will show *all* categories, i.e. the ones
that exist in English. This makes it possible to translate everything, but you have

column125:
08/Feb/22 3:06 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;There’s something kind of odd going on with this.

# When I do a search for “Darkleer ♦ The Disciple”, I get exactly one matching tag.
# Similarly, when I do a search for “Dave ♦ Sawbuck”, I get exactly one matching tag.
# When I search for “Darkleer ♦”, I get no results whatsoever.
# When I search for just “♦”, I get 100 tags, all of which have a ♦ in them. But none of the matching tags is either “Darkleer ♦ The Disciple” or “Dave ♦ Sawbuck”. In fact, none of the tags at all have the word “Darkleer” in them.
# When I search for “Dave ♦”, I get an assortment of 12 tags, all of which have both the word “Dave” and the ♦ symbol in them. But none of those 12 tags are the “Dave ♦ Sawbuck” tag.

I’m wondering if one of the Elasticsearch upgrades changed the way the tokenizer works, so that any tags indexed after the upgrade work fine, and any tags indexed before the upgrade don’t handle the ♦ character properly.

*EDIT:* On staging, unlike in production, searching for “Dave ♦” does include “Dave ♦ Sawbuck” in the search results. So if this isn’t an indexing issue, there’s something different about the ES configuration for staging vs. production.

*EDIT 2:* But the “Darkleer ♦ The Disciple” tag has the exact same behavior on staging as on production. So it’s not a staging vs. production difference.

*EDIT 3:* Yup, this is an indexing issue. Sarken reindexed “Dave ♦ Sawbuck” in production, and it’s now showing up in the “♦” and “Dave ♦” searches (in addition to the “Dave ♦ Sawbuck” search, where it always appeared).

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*

# Create a tag set that allows nominations
## Log in as the user who will own the tag set
## Browse > Tags >Tag Sets > New Tag Set
## Fill in a title
## Check “Currently taking nominations?”
## For “Fandom nomination limit” and “Freeform nomination limit” enter 20 (this is the maximum number you can allow)
## For “Character nomination limit,” enter 5
## Submit
## Make note of your tag set’s URL
# Nominate more than 30 of each tag type
## Follow the Nominate link
## Fill in all 20 slots for both fandoms and freeforms – you can do something like tag1, tag2, tag3
## Fill in a few characters for some fandoms
## Submit
## Log out
## Log in as a different user
## Go to your tag set’s URL
## Repeat steps 2a - 2c, although you only need to nominate 11 tags in each
# Review the nominations in your tag set
## Log in as the user from 1a
## Go to your tag set’s URL
## Follow the Review Nominations link

*What is the expected output? What do you see instead?*

Expect to be able to see all the nominations pending review.  

Instead, if there are more than 30 additional tags or 30 fandoms, only get 30 at random along with a blue notice banner that says, “There are too many nominations to show at once, so here's a randomized selection! Additional nominations will appear after you approve or reject some.” (Incidentally, the banner is sticky: if you go to the Review Nominations page and then click another link, e.g. the site name in the header, the notice banner will appear on the next page you access.) 

The listboxes for each tag type should be paginated using pagy ([AO3-6880|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/issues/AO3-6880]), with pagination links at the top and bottom. The heading should say “X - Y of Z Tag Type.” The pagination links should have anchors so, e.g., if you go to page 2 in the Additional Tags listbox, the Additional Tags listbox is at the top of your screen when the next page loads.

Also, the blue notice should be removed.

For now, we can sort by creation date ascending.

column1: Synned tags sometimes fail to get the media/fandom of the canonical tag
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3776
otwarchive v0.9.9.8

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Syn a new, unwrangled tag to an existing canonical tag
2. The synned tag should automatically add the media/fandom(s) of the canonical tag
(fandom tags add the media(s); character, relationship, and freeform tags add the fandom(s)).

This action is queued so slightly delayed (usually only 5-15 seconds, sometimes up
to a minute; when the tag is reloaded the fandoms/media will appear.)

However, sometimes this process seems to be dropped from the queue entirely, and the
media/fandom is never added. (This causes trouble because the tag will then just sit
in the unwrangled bins rather than moving to the appropriate media/fandom bin as expected;
and wranglers are used to synning and closing a tag without waiting around to double-check
that it's had the media/fandoms attached.)

There doesn't seem to be any consistency in which tags fail to get the media/fandom,
or when it happens. This has been an occasional problem since the fandom-adding was
queued; but since the Rails upgrade it's been happening much more frequently (when
I last wrangled it was about every 1 in 10 tags?)

Not sure if this is replicable in Test - I just tried with a dozen tags on Test and
they all worked fine; that may be just luck or else it's an issue specific to the Beta
servers?

However, if you use the center tag in the HTML editor and switch to the RTE, you cannot

attribute, which means it will not affect the center tag. So use align="center" instead

of browser, operating system, and word processor
http://code.google.com/p/otwarchive/issues/detail?id=3267

This also adds a button for video embeds, as discussed in the AD&T e-mail thread "Update
RTE?" from 11 August 2013. If you look at the [example editor on the TinyMCE site](http://www.tinymce.com/tryit/full.php),
there are two tabs in the Insert/Edit Video popup. The General tab is geared toward
uploads, which isn't something we offer. The Embed tab is where you paste the embed
code just like you'd paste it into our HTML/plain text editor. Naturally, there's not
a way to configure TinyMCE to only use the Embed tab on the Media plugin.

from Word is identical to pasting from everywhere else (this is true in our current
version as well, but the button is still there). If wanted, I can add a plain Paste
button (there are also Copy and Cut buttons) so we don't rely on users knowing the
keyboard shortcut for pasting.

numbers, underscores, no spaces)"

2) Change the tooltip from "The name can consist only of ASCII letters (a-z, A-Z),
numbers and underscores" to "The name can consist only of ASCII letters (a-z, A-Z),
numbers and underscores, and cannot contain spaces."

3) Change the error message from "Name must begin and end with a letter or number;
it may also contain underscores but no other characters." to "Name must begin and end
with a letter or number; it may also contain underscores.  It may not contain any other
characters, including spaces."

worse. The following behavior is also true on Beta right now:

- For all kudos, the number in the work blurb only updates every 5 minutes

hold up the deploy right now.

to be seen.

Would like one more set of eyes on this, then we can VOT with a new issue for the caching.

20/Oct/13 5:38 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;There's a Chrome bug where it treats anything inside <noscript> as just a string of
text immediately after the user turns off JavaScript:

http://code.google.com/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=232410

https://code.google.com/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=235158

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/15800526/how-do-i-display-html-within-chromes-noscript-tag

We could work around this by not using <noscript>, and instead making anything we currently
put inside <noscript> visible by default and hidden via JavaScript. It's not a bad
idea, and there are only ten instances of <noscript> on the Archive. The downside is
users who are on slower connections will most likely get flashes of those elements
before the JavaScript loads and the elements are hidden. 

Or we could not do anything, since this is going to be an issue for coders and testers
much more than for regular users, who are probably not going to be switching JavaScript
on and off in Chrome every time they load a page.- **Status changed**: `New`
