column1: Race conditions can create duplicate or invalid signups that cause assignments to crash
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3815

otwarchive v0.9.10.7

A signup can be created that is a duplicate or invalid by the rules of the challenge.


This issue is essentially impossible to reproduce because it only occurs if there's
a hiccup in the server, generally due to extremely high volume of signups. It happens
occasionally during Yuletide signups. The most common cause of an invalid signup is
a duplicate of an existing prompt. 

This isn't a case that can be avoided easily because the rules of each challenge are
substantially different and there isn't a SQL condition that can be put in the database
to prevent the insertion of these Rails-invalid records. 

Afterwards, if not cleaned up, the duplicate signup will cause doubled assigning and
the invalid signups will cause assignments to crash (and even worse, silently, because
they are running in the background).

I think probably the best imperfect solution would be to put a check for validity on
the individual signup "show" page. This is the page the user gets redirected to from
signup creation. It could check just that user's signups for a duplicate signup for
the same challenge, or if the new signup is invalid, and possibly clean it up right
then. 

The downside of this is that it violates the RESTful concept where going to a "show"
page should not change anything. But given that this is not something where we can

column121:
27/Oct/13 11:18 AM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;The symptom of this happening generally include that assignments die some part of the
way through. The mods can load up the matching page and see some assignments listed,
but it doesn't progress any further. 

There are two workarounds, one that the mods can do themselves:

1) Find the invalid signup through the archive front end. The most likely case is a
duplicate signup, so check for someone's name listed twice in the signups. Delete whichever
duplicate is invalid. If the problem is still occurring, go through all signups and
check for too many offers/requests or too many tags in each one. (A relative shortcut
for this is to edit and attempt to save -- if the signup is invalid it won't save.)

2) If a senior coder is available, here's the console workaround: 
collection = Collection.find_by_name("collection_name_here")
collection.signups.select {|s| !s.valid?}.collect {|s| [s.id, s.errors.full_messages.join(',
')]}

This will list all the signups by id and the validation errors on them. The mods can
then look at the specific signups at: 

http://ao3.org/collectons/COLLECTION_NAME/signups/SIGNUP_ID

01/Sep/20 7:33 PM;557058:f99670ac-6f0b-469b-bdfb-a9817a67932f;Repurposed this issue for its most likely cause: user-agent strings that are too long. Solutions we have discussed:

*Stop saving user agent strings for comments*
Not viable. We save user agents on comments so comments can be marked as spam later. Akismet requires user agents in all spam reports.

*Use a fallback user agent string if the real one is too long*
e.g. {{AO3-hand-spam}}. This is an easy fix. Unknown whether it will make spam detection less accurate.

*Introduce some code the hack down the length of the user agent string so it won't be too big for the column*
This is an easy fix, however, we risk polluting our Akismet dataset and making spam detection less accurate.

*Make the column able to handle longer user agent strings*
This is the lawful good fix, which requires a database migration on the big comments table. However:
- There's no max limit for user agent strings, someone will exceed whatever limit we set.
- "If strict SQL mode is not enabled and you assign a value to a BLOB or TEXT column that exceeds the column's maximum length, the value is truncated to fit and a warning is generated." ([MySQL docs on BLOB/TEXT|https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/blob.html]).

03/Sep/20 8:39 PM;557058:bb48f715-7c87-43a5-81b8-a60c77a4c45b;Are we running an nginx proxy in front (I feel like I’ve seen that mentioned somewhere)?  There should be a configurable max header size in that case which could act as an upper bound to user agent length.  Default is 8KB I believe, but could be decreased to help control this.

Side note that Google may start freezing most of the values in user-agent reasonably soon (for Chrome anyway): [https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/blink-dev/c/-2JIRNMWJ7s|https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/blink-dev/c/-2JIRNMWJ7s|smart-link] 

So who knows how the effectiveness of user-agent as signal for spam detection might be affected.
column130:
05/Sep/20 10:00 PM;557058:f99670ac-6f0b-469b-bdfb-a9817a67932f;Yeah, we run an nginx reverse proxy. nginx has [the {{large_client_header_buffers}} directive|https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_core_module.html#large_client_header_buffers], which I don't think we should use, considering it will also cap the size of our cookies.

Freezing user agent strings looks promising. Maybe this is one of those issues we can simply wait out. :)

they have found is to de-canonize and re-canonize the tags). 

A related issue is occurring as well, with tags that are initially syns or subtags
of other tags: after removing a tag as a sub, the works sometime remain in the metatag,
even weeks or months later. And sometimes the tags can't be subbed again, because the
archive says they're already subbed, even though both tag edit pages disagree.  Basically,
the archive seems to have "hidden" metatag relationships that do not appear on the
tag edit pages.  Hidden parent/child relationships are an old issue but usually those
are impossible relationships that have no place to be displayed (e.g. a tag having
a child tag of the wrong category) - these are normal wrangling relationships that
function normally, but are invisible to wranglers, and cannot be wrangled.

This canonical tag was accidentally synned to another tag; when it was de-synned and
made back into a metatag canonical, most of its subtags could not be added:
http://archiveofourown.org/tags/Franklin
If you try to add any of the Franklin subtags from the metatag page there is no error
message; they simply do not appear on the tag edit page. If you try from a subtag's
page - e.g. try to add the Franklin metatag on the tag Stephen Franklin - it gives
an error message:
Sorry! We couldn't save this Character because:
Meta taggings is invalid
The Franklin tag works list still brings up works tagged with the pre-existing subtags
(including newly posted works), as if they are still subtags, though they are not shown
on the tag edit page or public tag pages.

Something causes SPN works to appear in the Animal Transformation results, even though
they have no Animal Transformation or anything similar attached:
http://archiveofourown.org/tags/Animal%20Transformation/works

Sometimes tags that are erroring can be resynned or resubbed a few days later.

Use only one declaration per property per ruleset
The CSS parser we use retains only one declaration for each property, meaning that
rulesets like
      .my-class {
        background: -moz-linear-gradient(top, #1e5799 0%, #2989d8 50%, #207cca 51%,
#7db9e8 100%);
        background: -o-linear-gradient(top, #1e5799 0%,#2989d8 50%,#207cca 51%,#7db9e8
100%);
        background: -webkit-linear-gradient(top, #1e5799 0%,#2989d8 50%,#207cca 51%,#7db9e8
100%);
      }
    
will have all but the last background declaration removed (so your gradient would only
show up in WebKit browsers). To avoid losing declarations with repeated properties,
split each one into its own ruleset, like so:
      .my-class { background: -moz-linear-gradient(top, #1e5799 0%, #2989d8 50%, #207cca
51%, #7db9e8 100%); }
      .my-class { background: -o-linear-gradient(top, #1e5799 0%,#2989d8 50%,#207cca
51%,#7db9e8 100%); }
      .my-class { background: -webkit-linear-gradient(top, #1e5799 0%,#2989d8 50%,#207cca
51%,#7db9e8 100%); }
    
If you are new to CSS, here are the basics:
A line of CSS code looks pretty much like this: selector {property: value;}

The selector is either the name of an HTML tag (like body or h1), or it can be an id
or class that has been set on a tag. The property is what you want to change in the
contents of that tag (for instance the font size), and the value is what you want to
set it to.

Examples:

Inside the "body" tag, set the font size slightly larger than the baseline: body {font-size:
1.1em;}
Inside any tags with the id "header", set the background color to purple: #header {background-color:
purple}
Inside any tags with the class "meta", make the text blink: (we do not advise this)
.meta {font-style: blink}

at all. If it’s just fixing the position: fixed skin scenario in that issue, we can
probably take it out, since we’ve removed the ability to use position: fixed in a work

just to stop vertical overflow? We have the collection side bar on some works, so possibly
not."

*Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3875*

*What archive revision are you testing on?* otwarchive v0.9.12.6

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*

# Make one of testy's collections moderated.
# With another user, post a work to that collection.
# Try to find it with the same user who created the work.

*What is the expected output? What do you see instead?*

The work isn't anywhere – not in the regular Works list (users/username/works), not in the Works in Collections list (users/username/works/collected), not in the collected works page (users/username/collection_items). 

I would expect it to be in the Works in Collections list as the user might want to edit it (for example, in an extreme case, to take it out of the Collection! If the Moderator never approves it or rejects it (because, for example, they left fandom), the user can't ever find the work using the Archive.

Particular behaviours:

* You can see the work when you've just posted it 
* You can access it if you've a direct link
* This is not a problem for collections that aren't anonymous or unrevealed, in which case the work appears in the regular works list, and not in the works in collections list

[http://archiveofourown.org/works/1101703|http://archiveofourown.org/works/1101703]

*Notes*

{quote}ticking instant (AO3 Contributor)  20:47
By the way, for 3867, is the goal to have works in moderated collections to show up on the "Works in Collections" page? Because I think that would require either not using ES for that page, or adding an extra field that mostly behaves like the current collection_ids field, but also includes unapproved collections. (Which would require reindexing all works, I think.)

sarken  20:49
That was the original goal according to the issue, but we can rethink if we have to

ticking instant (AO3 Contributor)  20:51
It makes sense, it's just not as simple as changing only the collection items page.{quote}

*Testing*

First, let’s make sure you can update and see collection items' statuses:

# Create a collection. It doesn’t need to be moderated, unrevealed, or anonymous, but it can be.
# As the same user, add at least one work and one bookmark to the collection through whatever means you like: posting a new work, inviting one, editing an existing bookmark, whatever.
# Now, from your collection, open the “Manage Items” page in one tab.
# In another tab, go to Hi, username > My Dashboard > My Collections > Manage Collection Items.
# Use the select (dropdown) menus on these pages to change the status of your collection items in a variety of ways, and then make sure they appear on the expected pages, and that the select menus reflect their current statuses. *For example,* because you added or invited your own items to a collection you own, they should start off on the “Approved” page for both the collection and the user. If, from your collection’s “Manage Items” page, you change the item to “Unreviewed by collection moderators,” it should then move to the “Awaiting Collection Approval” page for both the collection and  the user (you’ll have to refresh as the user).  

Now let’s make sure using an item’s “Remove” option works:

# Add some more items or more moderators to the collection. The point is you want to make sure you have a mod who does not own at least one of the works and bookmarks.
# A user who is on their “Manage Collection Items” page should be able to use the “Remove” checkbox to remove an item of any status from a collection.
# A collection moderator who is on their collection’s “Manage Items” should be able to use the “Remove” checkbox to remove an item from their collection _as long as the item is not on the “Rejected by User” page_ (because we don’t want moderators inviting works after the creator has decided they don’t want them in the collection). However! If you are both the collection moderator and the owner of the item, you should be able to remove it from the “Rejected by User” page.

Now let’s make sure the “Unrevealed” and “Anonymous” checkboxes and the select menus look reasonably okayish. Please note your device/operating system/browser, including version numbers:

# As the moderator, go to the “Collection Settings” page and make the collection anonymous and/or unrevealed. (Note that this doesn’t automatically make the works anonymous or unrevealed.)
# Now go to the “Manage Items” page and see if the newly-added “Anonymous” and/or “Unrevealed” checkboxes and the select menus look okay.
# As a user with items in that collection, go to your “Manage Collection Items” page, locate the items, and make sure the newly-added “Anonymous” and/or “Unrevealed” checkboxes and the select menus look okay. (They’ll be disabled for you.)
# Apply the “Reversi” skin and repeat steps 2 and 3.

Please also check that the "invited" link in the confirmation message you get when inviting someone else's work to your collection goes to the correct page!

*Deploy notes*

This has changes to Reversi, so an admin will need to log in and paste [Reversi from the file|https://github.com/sarken/otwarchive/blob/3fa4fbbd37233fa5c0c2109163371741ecf16fbe/public/stylesheets/masters/reversi/reversi_site_screen_.css] +before+ we deploy. If we do it after, james will have to recache the skins again.

column1: Gift emails after challenge reveal not going out: reveal queue code needs refactor
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3876
What archive revision are you testing on? (See the version label in
the footer, for example v0.8.13.8.)
otwarchive v0.9.12.6

Elz sez:

  def reveal!
    async(:reveal_collection_items)
    async(:send_reveal_notifications)
  end

- if we have more than one collection queue (which we do), there's no guarantee that
those will run in the right order	
- and if the second one runs first, nothing will go out
- that could be why we haven't run into it in testing 
- (there's only one queue in test)
- if that's the problem, it's easy to fix
- just make one async job and put both actions in it
- it's more efficient that way anyway

Testers will need to make sure that gift emails are still going out after a challenge

column123:
15/Jul/19 5:40 AM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;I suspect this might be happening because [the default scope on Bookmarks orders by ID|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/dd6ca1180f875ae8def2b21b7b78adc68c805c1f/app/models/bookmark.rb#L16]:

{code}  default_scope -> { order("bookmarks.id DESC") } # id's stand in for creation date{code}

Further calls to {{order}} don’t override the order set by this scope; they add to it. So calling {{order('RAND()')}} in a bookmark query generates SQL with {{ORDER BY bookmarks.id DESC, RAND()}}. That results in bookmarks being sorted by ID, with any ties broken randomly. (Though I’m not sure how that could show the oldest bookmarks, instead of the newest ones.)

I think the fix is either to delete the default scope (and fix up any queries that rely on that default order), or update any queries that order bookmarks to call {{reorder}} instead of {{order}}.

18/Feb/19 11:17 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;One more tiny tweak: [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/3527]

h2. Purpose
From the [ebook-convert documentation|https://manual.calibre-ebook.com/generated/en/ebook-convert.html#cmdoption-ebook-convert-toc-threshold]:

{quote}\-\-toc-threshold
If fewer than this number of chapters is detected, then links are added to the Table of Contents. Default: 6

{quote}
So basically what was happening was, if the work had fewer than four chapters (because four actual chapters, plus preface and afterword equals six) and it had work or chapter endnotes, you'd end up with "notes" as a TOC entry.

This was weird, since it's not like we were also adding entries for the beginning notes or summary. It was even weirder if you had multiple end notes because only _one_ of the endnotes would be linked because, by default, ebook-convert does not allow you to have two TOC entries with the same name.

So anyway, we're going to stop it from turning "notes" into a TOC entry.

h2. Testing Instructions
Post a work with at least one endnote and less than four chapters and make sure "notes" does not appear in the download file's table of contents.

19/Jan/14 2:57 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;This is just an on/off setting for us, but if we intend to make a report to TinyMCE,
it's probably going to be helpful to check the default behavior of your browser's spell
check in dealing with pasted text, because that varies. Spell check should, however,
work when starting a new work in the RTE without pasting.

Here's what I did to get a baseline for how spell check works in a given browser:

1. Find a text area on another site, e.g. the comment field here.
2. Paste my text and note whether spell check runs.
3. Find a text area on our site, e.g. the summary field on our post new form.
4. Paste my text and note whether spell check runs.

To start, I'm working with (a formatted version of) "Thes is texed with some typos.
Theyre kinda bad onez."

In Firefox 26 on OS X 10.9.1, spell check runs on pasted text here, on the summary
field, and in the RTE. 

In Safari 7, spell check does not run on pasted text here, on the summary field, but
it does pick up the first misspelled word in the RTE if it's the first word on the
sentence. Otherwise, if I paste the text "This is texed with some typos. Theyre kinda
bad onez." it does not run.

In Chrome 31, spell check runs on pasted text here, on the summary field, and it runs
partway in the RTE immediately upon pasting, and the rest of the way if you click outside
the RTE text area.

In Opera 16, spell check runs on pasted text here, on the summary field, and it runs
partway in the RTE immediately upon pasting, and the rest of the way if you click outside
the RTE text area.

Browser spell check behavior also varies depending on the length of the text and the
number of typos. If I paste ~700 words of lorem ipsumy nonsense with a bit of proper
English thrown in...

Firefox 26: spell check goes through about 3/4 of the text upon pasting here or in
the summary field. It goes through the first couple of sentences in the RTE. Clicking
outside the RTE text area does nothing. Toggling to the HTML editor and then back to
the RTE makes it run exactly as far as it does here or in the summary field.

Safari 7: spell check does not run upon pasting text here, in the summary field, or
in the RTE.

Chrome 31: spell check runs on the entire text upon pasting here or in the summary
field. It picks up a few random things in the RTE. Clicking outside the RTE text area
does nothing. Toggling to the HTML editor and then back to the RTE does nothing.

Opera 16: spell check runs on the entire text upon pasting here or in the summary field.
It runs through the first sentence or so of the RTE. Clicking outside the RTE text
area does nothing. Toggling to the HTML editor and then back to the RTE does nothing.
Clicking inside the RTE after toggling between the editors finds the same errors that
are highlighted here or in the summary field.

column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3891
What archive revision are you testing on? (See the version label in

v0.9.12.6

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Post a work to a fandom
2. Import a work, tagging it for the same fandom
3.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

Expect to see the imported work at the top of the fandom tag's work listing, since
it was posted more recently.  Instead, it may appear before the earlier work.

Please use labels and text to provide additional information.

This issue seems to involve the imported work getting assigned a date, but not a time,
so it ends up with the default time of noon.  This seems to happen both for works imported
from sites such as LJ, from which the importer can scrape a date, and sites with no
date available.  (Works imported from LJ are backdated to their LJ posting date, but
if that date is "today", it's noticeable that the work doesn't get the right time.)

The problem is much more apparent in a popular fandom, where many pages of works may
be posted in a day.

Ticket from a user experiencing the issue: https://otw.16bugs.com/projects/4911/bugs/293050
column119:
30/May/15 4:19 AM;557058:acee4fce-21cc-4291-8fa0-d813e774e099;This is indeed due to the fact that the StoryParser responsible for the import coerces
any date strings it finds into a Date object rather than a DateTime one. This might
therefore be fixable simply by changing one to the other.
column120:
22/Jun/15 12:42 AM;557058:acee4fce-21cc-4291-8fa0-d813e774e099;Further poking reveals that the reason the StoryParser uses a Date rather than a DateTime
is that although the 'revised_at' field on the work itself is a DateTime, the 'published_at'
field in individual chapters is a Date. When importing multiple chapters, the StoryParser
sets the date in 'revised_at' by copying over the date from the last chapter it imported.
If it parses the incoming date for the chapter as a DateTime, this process fails and
the 'revised_at' field on the work doesn't get updated at all.

21/Feb/16 10:56 AM;557058:77351d0c-19f2-456d-8c3f-39bc145cb6dd;1) Posted a work at ~8:20 HST (UTC -10)
2) Posted another work at 8:27
3) Created a test work with the text "Date: 2016-02-21 08:26:00" at the top
4) Imported the test work

Test work appeared in work listings _below_ the two other works when sorting by the default "Date Updated"

5) Removed the date line from the test work and imported again

Work appeared below all three works

If I sorted by "Date Posted", the works appear in the order I posted/imported them (ignoring the file date).

This doesn't seem fixed, if I'm understanding correctly?
column126:
23/Feb/16 1:40 AM;557058:85e7b59e-f3ad-4868-81c9-145d4251c741;Unfortunately, the issue Lady Oscar noticed appears to be due to time zones. Although this pull request correctly detects the time on an external work, there is no time zone information, so the Archive interprets the imported time as being its default of EST (GMT-5). So to illustrate, using the equivalent UTC date-time:

1. Manually posted in the HST time zone with a date-time of "2016-02-21 08:20:00" = UTC "2016-02-21 18:20:00"
2. Manually posted in the HST time zone with a date-time of "2016-02-21 08:27:00" = UTC "2016-02-21 18:27:00"
3. Imported with a date-time of "2016-02-21 08:26:00", which is interpreted as EST = UTC "2016-02-21 13:26:00"

Because the Archive can't tell the time on the latter is supposed to be in the HST time zone, the imported work has an earlier date-time than the manually posted ones.

There is no solution to this problem, as we can't detect time zones in external works that don't contain them, so this is likely to cause more confusion than it resolves. The pull request was reverted and this being closed as Won't Fix.

column1: Remove expensive counts from work index caching check
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3893
Currently, when you hit a works index page for a tag, pseud, user or collection, we
cache the results but do some expensive database counts to check whether or not the
cache should be expired. Instead of doing that, we want to expire the cache keys when
the data is updated.

Testing cheat sheet:

Stuff that should expire the works index cache for a tag:
-a new work is posted with that tag
-a work with that tag is updated
-a work is edited to add the tag
-a chapter is added to a work with that tag
-a work with that tag is deleted
-a work with that tag is edited to remove the tag
-the tag gains or loses a synonym
-the tag gains or loses a subtag

Stuff that should expire the works index cache for a user or pseud:
-the user posts a new work
-the user updates a work
-the user adds a chapter to a work
-the user deletes a work
-the user is added as an author to an existing work
-the user is removed as an author to an existing work
-the user orphans a work
-a work by the user is added to an anonymous or unrevealed collection
-a work by the user is removed from an anonymous or unrevealed collection
-a collection that includes a work by the user is changed to no longer be anonymous
or unrevealed

Stuff that should expire the works index cache for a collection:
-a work is added to the collection
-a work in the collection is updated
-a chapter is added to a work in the collection
-a work is removed from the collection
-a work in the collection is deleted
-the collection stops being anonymous or unrevealed

19/Jan/14 5:56 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;We don't let users force links to open in a new window -- the sanitizer strips the target

in the text.)

and for ease of maintainability, we don't modify the TinyMCE source code. As you noted,

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Create a collection as a Gift Exchange or Prompt Meme, or edit an existing collection
to make it one
2. Decide you don't want your collection to be a challenge anymore
3. Go to your collection's Profile and choose "Challenge Settings"
4. Choose "Delete Challenge"

 Instead, while signup, assignments, etc. pages vanish, the collection still identifies

an update.

Ticket reporting the issue: https://otw.16bugs.com/projects/4911/bugs/295687

This is especially problematic for ex-Prompt Memes, as Prompt Memes don't have a "Post
to Collection" button, and deleting the Prompt Meme from a challenge doesn't make this
button re-appear.

column1: Add mass-wrangle to fandom capability to fandom pages
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3911 Currently character/relationship/freeform tags can only be added to a fandom from the mass wrangle pages here: http://archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings?show=characters There is no mass-wrangling capability from the specific fandom /wrangle pages (where the majority of wrangling is performed). For example, this page: http://archiveofourown.org/tags/Homestuck/wrangle?show=freeforms&status=unwrangled shows all unwrangled tags used on works tagged with the Homestuck fandom. Most of these tags should be wrangled into either Homestuck or No Fandom. However, there is no way to batch-add them to either fandom; wranglers instead have to open and edit each tag individually, which is time-consuming and greater stress on the servers. We want the mass-wrangle function added to the individual /wrangle pages for fandoms, such as this one: http://archiveofourown.org/tags/Homestuck/wrangle?show=characters so that tags can be wrangled directly into a fandom. Checkboxes to the left of the tags should be added to mark which tags to wrangle, as shown on the mockup. This feature only needs to be added to the /wrangle pages for Fandom tags (chars/rels/freeforms also have /wrangle pages, but they're not commonly used by wranglers.) (This feature is part of the general overhaul of wrangling pages outlined on issue 3531.)

reindex queue when their hit counts are updated in the database. Instead, the work
blurb will be refreshed when some kind of feedback (e.g. comment, kudos) is left or

control.

column123:
08/Aug/23 9:54 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;Leaving this here to explain why it is, although the plan is to change the date behavior entirely (refer to the Epic Link on this issue), not fix this bug by itself. 

The date in the blurb is the {{revised_at}} date, which doesn't get changed when you change a work's posted state from false (draft) to true. 

The Published date in the meta is a whole different date: {{published_date = (chapter && work.preview_mode) ? chapter.published_at : work.first_chapter.published_at}} .

Date Posted always sorts by works' {{created_at}} dates (the date the work was actually created in the database), while Date Updated sorts by the {{revised_at}} dates (which _can_ be the {{created_at}} date, if the work was just posted from draft).

column1: Can't reorder tags on a work
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3945*

*What archive revision are you testing on?* 

v0.9.14.5

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*

# Post a work with some tags
# Edit the work and change the order of some or all of the tags
# Update, with or without previewing first

*What is the expected output?*

Expect to see your tag order changes. 

*What do you see instead?*

Instead, the tags are in their original order.

*Workaround*

Remove all tags, update the work, edit again, then re-add in the order you want.

*Notes*

This bug exists because tags (taggings) are not given a particular assigned order, as they would be if we used acts_as_list (which we use for ordering chapters, for example). Instead, tags are listed on the work in the same order they exist in and are retrieved from the database. Since reordering doesn’t destroy and recreate the taggings, this order doesn’t change.

*We have not yet decided on the proper approach to fix this.* Two possible solutions:

* Destroy and recreate all taggings when reordering. This might be somewhat inefficient (e.g. it might lead to works' filters being unnecessarily recalculated and the work being unnecessarily reindexed).
* Use acts_as_list to make the order explicit. This would require a migration of the taggings table, and we’d also need to determine whether tags should be ordered as one big list, or with each type (fandom, relationship, etc) as its own list (in case we want to change how tags are displayed in the blurb, e.g. make characters come before relationships).

column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3947
otwarchive v0.9.14.5

The "Matching" page would not load for many challenges after the potential matches
are generated. This is because the page included a list of all the potential givers
for each participant, sorted by quality of match, which for a challenge where users
can end up with many potential matches caused the page to take way too long to load,
so it timed out. 

In addition, the potential matches page was a hideous mess of inconsistent separate
forms for dealing with various issues, including users without potential matches, users
who didn't have an assignment, etc. 

The fixes: 

- The Matching page now looks like the attached screenshot. Tabs at the top allow the
moderator to see and handle each set of issues separately. (Each tab is paginated as
well, in case of a large challenge.) 

- You should be able to click on the assignment ID link to see the assignment in detail.


- You should be able to X out and change the recipient or the giver. Xing out the giver
will produce an autocomplete of all the potential matches for the recipient, Xing out
the recipient will produce an autocomplete of all the potential matches for the giver.


- Known issue: if you change BOTH, you can create an incompatible assignment -- there
isn't a way to avoid this without making this a live-edit form, which would be the
ideal but not in the cards at this time. 

- You can leave the fields blank to create an assignment with no recipient or no giver.


- The help file and brief instructions should hopefully be fairly clear! Suggestions
for edits welcome.

column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3959
Wranglers have the ability to mark certain unfilterable tags that cannot be wrangled
according to our guidelines, as "unwrangleable", such as seen here:

http://archiveofourown.org/tags/Homestuck/wrangle?show=characters&status=unwrangleable

Currently the only way to mark a tag unwrangleable is to go to the tag edit page for
the individual tag.

We want the ability to mass-mark multiple tags unwrangleable, or to unmark them as
unwrangleable, from fandom wrangle pages such as the page linked above.

Ideally, every tag on the table would have a check-box (as described here: https://code.google.com/p/otwarchive/issues/detail?id=3911
) and there would be a button somewhere on the page, "Mark Unwrangleable" allowing
all selected tags to be marked unwrangleable on the all, canonical, synonymous, and
unfilterable tables. There should be no such button on the "unwrangled" table, since
unwrangled (not yet placed in a fandom) tags should not be marked unwrangleable.

On the unwrangleable table showing the tags which have been marked unwrangleable, the
button should instead be "unmark unwrangleable", and allow wranglers to mass-unmark
tags that they no longer want to have marked unwrangleable.

(This feature is part of the general overhaul of wrangling pages outlined on issue
3531.)

column1: Get rid of tags in collections links
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3961

*How to reproduce:*

As described in AO3-3345, we have the following problem:

1. Go to a work in a collection from the collection page - make sure that the link
is to ao3.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME/works/####
2. See that the tag links in the header box link to the tags within the collection
(e.g. ao3.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME/tags/TAGNAME/works rather than just ao3.org/tags/TAGNAME/works)
3. Go to the main listing of the work ao3.org/works/###
4. See that the tags still link to ao3.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME/tags/TAGNAME/works
rather than the expected ao3.org/tags/TAGNAME/works

This is because work blurbs are cached and shared between:

- ao3.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME/tags/TAGNAME/works
- ao3.org/tags/TAGNAME/works

We have a similar problem for child tag links, cached and shared between:

- ao3.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME/tags/TAGNAME
- ao3.org/tags/TAGNAME

*How to fix:*

This particular behaviour is due to caching, and is theoretically fixable. However,
after due consideration, we have decided that getting rid of the tags-in-collections
links altogether would be a better use of everyone's time and save Support from dealing
with users bewildered by being trapped in a collection.

Please consult the comments on AO3-3345 concerning the location of the code that
needs to be removed to eradicate the above behaviour. 
(And add tests to replicate the steps above to verify that the problem is forever gone)

Make sure that we don't break the tags-in-collections links on ao3.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME/tags and ao3.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME/fandoms.

column1: Commas in Chinese and Japanese scripts do not register as tag separators
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3965
Commas in some scripts do not register as commas, so users inadvertently make tags that
are actually several tags combined into one, for example:

百里屠苏，方兰生
http://archiveofourown.org/tags/%E7%99%BE%E9%87%8C%E5%B1%A0%E8%8B%8F%EF%BC%8C%E6%96%B9%E5%85%B0%E7%94%9F

(this should be two different tags, combined they are unwrangle-able)

This definitely happens with Chinese and Japanese language tags; it may happen with
other non-Roman alphabet scripts as well.

Users can still make separate tags by hitting "enter".

Unicode commas such as ， should either register as commas and cause a new tag to be
created, or else not be allowed in tags at all, to prevent this confusion.

When there's at least one work in a collection: http://test.ao3.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME
When there's at least one work fulfilling a prompt: http://test.ao3.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME/requests
When there's at least one draft for a user: http://test.ao3.org/users/USERNAME/works/drafts

When there's at least one bookmark in a collection: http://test.ao3.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME
When there's at least one bookmark on the site: http://test.ao3.org/bookmarks

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. View the source for the aforementioned pages, or
2. Log in
3. Hi, username! > My Dashboard
4. Skins
5. Create Skin
6. Fill in a title
7. Make a skin that attempts to style all the work blurbs, e.g. .work .blurb { background:
pink }
8. Submit
9. Use
10. Click around the site and notice there are places where the work blurb is not pink
11. Do the same for .bookmark .blurb, and also try some stuff with .listbox.group and
.index.group.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?
Our work indexes/listboxes should be class="[optional modifier] work index/listbox
group" and our bookmark indexes/listboxes should be "bookmark index/listbox group."
Some places said works or bookmarks, some places were missing group. This makes it
a pain in the backside to style things. "Hey, why aren't the bookmarks on the bookmark
index getting their purple background? Oh, because they don't have the group class,
so .group { background: purple; } isn't applying. And why aren't the works in history
displayed in Wingdings? Oh, because it's 'reading index group' instead of 'reading
work index group,' so .work .blurb { font-family: Wingdings; } isn't applied there."
This makes front end coders miserable, and it makes Support miserable when they try
to suggest CSS solutions to users only to have them not work as expected.

column1: Admin Posts translations can only belong to the last few posted admin posts
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3982
What archive revision are you testing on? otwarchive v0.9.14.55

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen: http://archiveofourown.org/admin_posts/####/edit

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Log in as admin
2. Go to a translation for a post
3. Check the "Is this a translation of another post?" drop down 

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

It only has the few last posts. This is reasonable when you're posting translations
in general (because we post translations of relevant, current posts).

Problem:

If we need to edit something in an old translation, the drop down gets 'unstuck' and
loses the connection to the old post, and to mark it as a translation we're forced
to mark it as a translation of one of the lasts posts.

This bad, because 1) the old post loses its translation, and 2) the translation gets
attached to a newer, incorrect post.

Note: the dropdown doesn't get unstuck if the post is one of the latest few that still
appear in it.

A way to fix it is to make the drop down keep the older post (avoid it getting unstuck).


Ideally, though, we would prefer to have a field in which we could input, for example,
the post number.

be undone!"

now the text is more like the text for editing and posting works.)

now it's visible for consistency with the edit work page and the chapter pages.)

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*
1. Log in

5. Fill in a title and some CSS
6. Submit
7. Look for the navigation in hopes of getting back to your skins
8. Edit
9. Look for the navigation in hopes of getting back to your skins

*What is the expected output? What do you see instead?*
On the skin show page:
- The navigation options used to be positioned on the right, like the rest of our navigation,
and the options were Work Skins, Public Skins, Remove Skin, My Skins, Create Skin.
- The options are currently positioned on the left and they are Revert to Default Skin
and Create Site Skin.
- I'd expect them to be Revert to Default Skin, My Site Skins, My Work Skins, and I'd
expect them to be on the right. I'd also expect them to be at the top of the home header
module, since that's where the actions usually are in such modules, and the icon should be directly after the h2. (See screen shot.)

On the skin edit, skin new, and skin new wizard page:
- The navigation options used to be Work Skins, Public Skins, Remove Skin, My Skins,
Create Skin, Use Wizard Instead?
- The options are currently Revert to Default Skin, Create Site Skin, Write Custom
CSS, Use Wizard. 
- I'd expect them to be Revert to Default Skin, Write Custom CSS, Use Wizard, My Site
Skins, My Work Skins.

(Note that Revert to Default only appears if you're using a skin, which is correct.)

Also, on all skin indexes:
- The copy currently says, "A site skin lets you change the way the Archive looks in
your browser, so you can customize your reading experience. You can use work skins
to customize the way your own works are shown to others."
- It's been brought to our attention that this is both fic-centric ("reading experience")
and assumes the user is browsing visually ("looks in your browser" -- work skins cannot
have different media types, so "shown" is probably okay), even though we also allow
users to create stylesheets for any media type: http://www.w3.org/TR/CSS21/media.html#media-types
- If you wanted to get ambitious, the My __ Skins indexes should probably be home zones
with spiffy header modules.
